items.title: Electrochemical biosensor can compute by itself
Soft-mode nonlinearities away from ferroelectric phase transition
authors: Payel Shee, Ipek Efe, Jingwen Li, Kshitij V. Goyal, Morgan Trassin, Shovon Pal
items.summary: Terahertz fields can drive soft lattice vibrations associated with ferroelectric phase transitions. These modes are hybrid in character, with a significant predominance of electronic oscillators and local-field effects. By investigating a strained paraelectric SrTiO3 using nonlinear terahertz spectroscopy, Shee et al. show that, though strong local-field effects sustain coherent nonlinear responses, the absence of polarization keeps the system in the perturbative regime of light-matter interaction. The findings offer insights into the role of polarization in controlling nonlinear lattice dynamics.

items.title: Physical understanding of dopant pair interaction and segregation energies in single-atom alloys
authors: Rui Qi, Yan Wang, Yujing Zhang, Sergey V. Levchenko, Xiaojuan Hu, Iftikhar Hussain, Zhong-Kang Han
items.summary: When do isolated dopants in single-atom alloys remain dispersed at surfaces or pair and segregate? Qi et al. combine first-principles calculations with interpretable data mining to identify how guest and host properties jointly govern these competing tendencies. The resulting physical rules guide large-scale alloy screening and connect materials discovery with an interpretable picture of dilute-alloy stability.

items.title: Ferroelectric Polarization Dynamics of HZO FeCAPs at a Verified Subnanosecond Time Scale
authors: Mor M. Dahan, Emanuel Ber, Florian Wunderwald, Guy Orlev, Edan Gefen, Ilya V. Karpov, Thomas Mikolajick, Sou-Chi Chang, Uwe Schroeder, and Eilam Yalon
items.summary: Abstract Ferroelectric random-access memory (FeRAM) based on the ferroelectric capacitor (FeCAP) offers a promising solution for next-generation embedded memory. In this Letter, we demonstrate subnanosecond ferroelectric polarization dynamics in HZO FeCAPs using an RF-compatible structure. By simultaneously measuring the electrode voltage and transient current under subnanosecond pulsing, we directly observe polarization dynamics with a temporal resolution below 100 ps. Our results demonstrate subnanosecond switching under directly monitored TE pulses with voltage amplitudes of 5 V in 8 nm-thick HZO capacitors with an area of 16 μm 2 . We also map switching kinetics for sub-10 ns pulse widths using this methodology. We further correlate polarization obtained from the dynamic current transient with the results from the postpulse readout scheme. Motivated by dynamic random-access-memory (DRAM) latency targets, these results establish a device-level benchmark for delivered subnanosecond switching in HZO FeCAPs and, together with a simplified nucleation-limited switching (NLS) analysis, define an effective ultrafast switching window for FeCAP evaluation.

items.title: Phonon-Activated Optical Transitions in Graphullerene Monolayers
authors: Aurélie Champagne, Antonios M. Alvertis, Yoann Olivier, Leeor Kronik, and Jeffrey B. Neaton
items.summary: Abstract Understanding the interplay between electronic states and lattice vibrations is crucial for predicting and engineering the electronic and optical properties of low-dimensional materials. Among these, graphullerene─a hybrid structure combining the planar characteristics of graphene with the curvature-induced properties of fullerene C 60 ─offers a unique platform for exploring vibronic coupling effects beyond the molecular limit. Here, using ab initio many-body perturbation theory and nonperturbative finite difference approaches, we calculate the renormalization of the quasiparticle (QP) and optical band gaps of graphullerene monolayers induced by nuclear motion. We find a renormalization of 0.22 eV for the QP gap and 0.33 eV for the optical gap at 300 K. We show that the large optical red shift predominantly arises from a Herzberg–Teller-like mechanism, in which zero-point nuclear motions dynamically reduce symmetry and activate otherwise forbidden vertical transitions at Γ.

items.title: Self-adaptive metasurface integrating sensing and active wave control for intelligent wireless communications
items.summary: Abstract The vision for future wireless networks extends far beyond mere connectivity, fostering spaces that autonomously perceive and adapt to the radio environment. Reconfigurable metasurfaces (RMSs) are designed to tailor wireless propagation through programmable electromagnetic responses. However, conventional RMSs, while assisting communication, lack integrated sensing and self-adaptive control capabilities and suffer from severe path loss along the transmitter-RMS-receiver link. Here we report a self-adaptive metasurface (SA-MS) that integrates sensing and active wave control within a unified platform. Each meta-atom integrates dual-biased PIN diodes and an embedded port, enabling 1-bit programmable reflection and in-band sensing. The sensed waveform is fed to a lightweight convolutional neural network that infers the direction of arrival with robustness against array mismatches. The acquired spatial information is then mapped through a physics-informed surrogate model to an amplitude-phase configuration that works in conjunction with the amplifier to enhance the wireless link. Real-world wireless communication experiments in dynamic environments validate the sensing, decision, and execution loop of SA-MS, with an average signal enhancement of 14.6 dB. This work paves the way for intelligent wireless spaces, where sensing and communication co-evolve at the physical layer.

items.title: Quantum melting and Pomeranchuk effect of zero-field Wigner solids
items.summary: Wigner solids and crystals are many-body phases of matter in which repulsive interactions between the charge carriers cause them to freeze into a solid. How Wigner solids compete or cooperate with integer and fractional quantum Hall liquids has been a long-standing open question. Here, we investigate this question for zero-field, electron and hole Wigner solids in cadmium arsenide quantum wells. In the low temperature limit, our results are consistent with a recent theoretical model [A. P. Reddy and L. Fu, Phys. Rev. B 113, L161403 (2026)] that proposes that the quantum Hall liquid can become energetically favored over the solid at low integer filling factors. Going beyond the low-temperature limit, we observe a re-entrant solid that emerges from the quantum Hall liquid. We explain this observation by considering the role of spin entropy, in close analogy with the zero-field Pomeranchuk effect, but appearing here at finite fields. The competition between quantum Hall liquids and Wigner solids is thus governed by both energy and entropy terms, giving rise to rich phase stability diagrams that result from the interplay between topology and correlations.

items.title: Pressure and Magnetic Field Control of Topology in Antiferromagnetic Bilayers
items.summary: Controlling band topology in magnetic semiconductors requires strategies that couple electronic structure to experimentally accessible degrees of freedom. Here we propose a cooperative approach based on pressure and magnetic reorientation in A-type antiferromagnetic bilayers. Antiparallel layer magnetizations suppress hybridization between exchange-polarized band-edge states, limiting their response to interlayer compression. A magnetic field that aligns the layer moments removes this spin mismatch, enabling pressure-enhanced hybridization to drive a band inversion. The magnetization direction then controls the symmetries of the inverted bands and whether spin--orbit coupling produces a Chern-insulating gap or symmetry-protected nodal crossings. First-principles calculations for bilayer CrSBr illustrate this mechanism within a compressed orthorhombic structural model. Out-of-plane magnetization yields a Chern insulator with a chiral edge state, whereas in-plane magnetization supports a two-dimensional Weyl semimetal with node-connecting edge states. Continuous spin canting further demonstrates how magnetic reorientation can drive the transition and stabilize the Chern phase before full magnetic saturation. Although material-specific transition conditions depend on electronic correlations and structural stability under compression, the underlying strategy identifies interlayer hybridization as a link between magnetic order and band topology. These results provide a design principle for externally tunable topological phases in layered antiferromagnetic semiconductors.

items.title: Fibonacci Non-Abelian Quantum Hall States with Pair Structure - a classification of chiral 2-cluster many-body wave-functions
items.summary: Fibonacci anyons support universal topological quantum computation. They have been proposed to emerge in fractional quantum Hall (FQH) systems, such as the filling-fraction $ν=\tfrac{2}{3}$ state described by an effective $SU(3)_2$ Chern-Simons theory, and the $ν=\tfrac{2}{5}$ state with a $3$-cluster structure (an $n$-cluster structure means that $n$-electron bound states form a Laughlin-type wave function of the form $(z^{(n)}_i-z^{(n)}_j)^m$). In this work, we systematically classify FQH wave functions $P(z_1,\ldots,z_N)$ in the $N\rightarrow\infty$ limit, through a generalized pattern of zeros (gPOZ) approach, where the wave function is determined by the leading order of zero along with the accompanying leading polynomial that develops as successive number of $z_i$'s are brought together. Within this approach, we obtain a $(ν,h,c)$-classification of wave functions with a $2$-cluster (pair) structure. Among these wave functions, those with $(h,c) = (\tfrac12,\tfrac12)$, $(\tfrac32,\tfrac{7}{10})$, $(3,\tfrac45)$ correspond to gapped FQH states with filling fraction $ν$ and edge-state chiral central charge $c+1$, while others with $c<0$ may be gapless. We find that even a $2$-cluster structure can give rise to Fibonacci statistics, for $(ν,h,c) = (\tfrac14,\tfrac32,\tfrac{7}{10})$, corresponding to the $(5,4)$ minimal model, and for $(ν,h,c) = (\tfrac17,3,\tfrac45)$, corresponding to the $(6,5)$ minimal model. We further construct an ideal $4$-body Hamiltonian whose ground state is the $(\tfrac14,\tfrac32,\tfrac{7}{10})$ state.

items.title: Solution of the Qubit Marginal Problem from Fermionic Representability
items.summary: Whether local reduced states are compatible with a global quantum state---the quantum marginal problem---is central to quantum information and simulation. Here we present a solution to the ensemble marginal problem for qubits based on the representability theory of fermions. Encoding each qubit as one fermion in two orbitals, we prove that the representable qubit marginals form an exposed face of the set of $N$-representable fermionic reduced density matrices, selected by the vanishing of every site-occupation variance. Complete hierarchies of fermionic representability conditions therefore transfer exactly to qubits. Applications to frustrated Heisenberg and transverse-field Ising rings show that the $(2,3)$-positivity conditions are exact at the Majumdar--Ghosh point and accurate to about 0.5% at criticality. Because the conditions hold for any quantum state, they also provide a framework for mitigating measurement errors on qubit-based quantum devices.

items.title: Regularized Neural Quantum States for Heisenberg Magnets
items.summary: We introduce an approach to solving locally ordered quantum spin systems using neural network quantum states. First, our approach rests on choosing a spin basis constructed from the magnetic texture of a classical or quantum reference state. Second, the method improves convergence and suppresses parameter-space drift through a regularized Riemannian gradient descent adapted to the quantum state geometry of the variational state manifold. Combining these techniques enables stable ground-state calculations for two- and three-dimensional chiral spin systems with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions. The resulting variational ground-state energies are competitive with those of high-fidelity density matrix renormalization group calculations and, for periodic and layered geometries, provide significantly tighter upper bounds on the ground-state energy.

items.title: Imaging spin entanglement with a scanning tunneling microscope
items.summary: Artificial spin arrays assembled on surfaces enable atomic-scale studies of quantum correlations. Here we establish a hierarchy of connections between spin inelastic electron tunneling spectroscopy (IETS) and entanglement in spin-$1/2$ systems. We first show that the number of spectroscopically active transitions in a spin-$1/2$ dimer serves as an entanglement witness. Using the leading-order tunneling conductance for the tip placed on spin $i$, $dI(i)/dV$, we then relate spectral moments $\mathcal{M}^{(n)}(i)=\int V^n(d^2I(i)/dV^2)\,dV$ to quantum correlations. The zeroth moment probes the one-tangle in systems with a gapped, nondegenerate ground state. For rotationally invariant Heisenberg systems, the first moment yields thermal spin correlators $\langle\boldsymbol S(i)\cdot\boldsymbol S(j)\rangle$, enabling reconstruction of nearest-neighbor concurrence and spatial imaging of entanglement in spin chains. It also provides access to the internal energy and magnetic specific heat, both usable as entanglement witnesses. Applying this approach to experimental IETS data from nanographene spin chains, we find good agreement with theory. We further discuss how the second moment probes longer-range correlations and the inverse moment relates to local spin susceptibility. For spin-$1/2$ trimers, we connect inter-multiplet inelastic spectral weight to genuine tripartite entanglement quantified by the concurrence fill. Finally, we reconcile the local character of IETS with its sensitivity to nonlocal entanglement through an analogy with digital quantum circuits, where Hamiltonian evolution implements multiqubit operations. These results establish IETS as a tool for quantifying and imaging entanglement in engineered on-surface spin systems.

items.title: Hall resistance under a non-Hermitian linear potential
items.summary: We investigate how a non-Hermitian linear perturbation modifies Landau states and Hall transport, combining an exact continuum solution with numerical tight-binding calculations on a finite square lattice. The analytical solution yields energy branches with a complex linear Stark shift. A conserved non-Hermitian guiding-center operator identifies coherent states and determines the orbit center through its eigenvalue. The continuum model admits states with balanced gain and loss whose energies remain real at any perturbation strength. Finite-lattice calculations support the Landau-level structure and exhibit eigenvalue coalescences followed by the emergence of imaginary parts, consistent with exceptional points. Finally, transport calculations at a fixed injection energy show a shift of the Hall resistance plateaus moving them linearly from the von Klitzing constant.

items.title: Fine-tuned atomistic foundation model for accurate sodium-carbon chemistry in Na-ion batteries
items.summary: Atomistic foundation models have emerged as a promising route to DFT-level accuracy for materials simulation with complex chemical environments. However, their reliability across competing bonding regimes and, more importantly, how complex bonding affects predictions of material properties remain unclear. Among materials with competing bonding regimes, sodium storage in hard carbon poses a substantial challenge. Hard carbon features diverse local structural motifs, including defective and curved graphitic regions, amorphous regions, and closed/open pores. Motivated by its importance for Na-ion batteries, we systematically evaluate existing pretrained foundation models based on the MACE architecture across different local Na/C motifs. We find that the pretrained models fail to accurately capture Na-Na and Na-C interactions for metallic Na clusters on graphene. To recover a DFT-level energetic description, we employ targeted fine-tuning, showing that it can describe the energetic stability of local motifs and achieve sufficient transferability to unseen Na/C environments. With the developed fine-tuned model, we establish a correlation between closed-pore radius in hard carbon and plateau voltage, showing that the small pores contribute at larger voltages than large ones, suggesting thus how the developed fine-tuned foundation model can link atomistic information with materials design for complex bonding environments.

items.title: Dissipation as a Resource for Entanglement via High-Spin Mediator Purification
items.summary: We study entanglement generation between two spin qubits mediated by a single, thermally mixed, high-spin ($S=5/2$) magnetic impurity, using the Lindblad master equation to compare coherent and dissipative control of the mediator. We show that no coherent drive, however strong or resonant, can purify the mediator beyond its thermal value --- a direct consequence of unitary evolution exactly preserving state purity --- while a dissipative channel purifies it up to the limit set by the optical pumping cycle itself, $\mathrm{Tr}[ρ_M^2]\approx0.8$. Modeling this channel with rates fixed by the measured optical pumping of a single Mn spin, we find that the entanglement it enables is not monotonic in the pump strength: it peaks at a finite rate and then decreases, since the same channel leaks decoherence to the qubits through the coupling that mediates their entanglement. At the experimental pumping rate, a single $80$ns pulse purifies the mediator, the resulting polarization persists for a timescale three orders of magnitude longer than the entangling dynamics, and the first-recurrence negativity rises from $0.18$ to $0.64$ at $12$K, remaining above $0.6$ up to $30$K. These results establish dissipation, not as noise to be suppressed, but as the very resource that makes robust entanglement generation possible.

items.title: Intrinsic Wannier Functions for Hamiltonian downfolding
items.summary: Downfolding ab initio material band structure into a low-energy subspace spanned by orbitals of specified atomic character, a procedure known as Wannier downfolding, is a common task in the simulation of complex materials. We introduce the Intrinsic Wannier Function (IWF) method to Wannierize bands with given atomic character. The method is non-iterative and requires only a single dimensionless parameter to disentangle bands. In benchmarks on silicon, graphene, and the three-band model of a mercury cuprate, we show that Intrinsic Wannier Functions provide high quality downfolded band structures compared to those from standard approaches such as Maximally Localized Wannier Functions, the Selected Columns of the Density Matrix method, and Projectability-Disentangled Wannier Functions. Further, their straightforward implementation and robustness position Intrinsic Wannier Functions as a general and useful tool for Wannier downfolding in materials electronic structure and in high-throughput applications.

items.title: Machine learning of strength surfaces enables high regularization length phase-field fracture
items.summary: Classical phase-field models of brittle fracture capture toughness-controlled crack growth but not the material's strength surface, which governs crack nucleation. The theory of Kumar et al. (2020) incorporates the strength surface through a nucleation driving force, and Chockalingam (2025) derived this driving force for arbitrary strength surfaces described by $n$ material parameters, with which the phase-field strength surface (PFSS) converges to the material strength surface as the regularization length $\varepsilon \to 0$ and matches it exactly at $n$ chosen states for any $\varepsilon$. In practice, however, the strength surface must be supplied as an analytic form chosen and calibrated case by case, and for the widely used analytic surfaces ($n=2$) accurate strength reproduction requires $\varepsilon$ commensurate with the Irwin characteristic length $l_{ch}$, imposing prohibitive mesh requirements for large structures. We introduce a neural-network (NN) strength function that is learned directly from strength data, is physics-constrained by construction, and provides far more calibration parameters than analytic surfaces; the calibration is generalized to any number of strength states and to enforce openness in chosen directions. A single architecture captures synthetic data from the Mohr-Coulomb, Drucker-Prager, Mogi-Coulomb and 3D Hoek-Brown surfaces and experimental data for graphite, natural rubber and styrene-butadiene rubber. The resulting PFSS is accurate up to $\varepsilon = 10\,l_{ch}$, whereas that of the exact analytic surfaces performs comparatively poorly even at $\varepsilon = 0.5\,l_{ch}$. Finite-element simulations validate the theory across fracture regimes. By decoupling strength fidelity from the regularization length, the approach substantially reduces the mesh resolution required for phase-field fracture simulations of large structures.

items.title: Topological phase diagram of an extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model with negative coupling
items.summary: Recently, an extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model with three atoms per unit cell has been experimentally realized in perovskite exciton-polariton micropillars. A distinctive feature of this system is that the second and third bands undergo a topological transition through a band crossing at the wave vector $k=0$, associated with a negative coupling. In this work, we analytically determine the phase diagram of the model as a function of the on-site energy splitting and the ratio of intercell to intracell hopping amplitudes. We identify seven regions in this lane, with four distinct topological phases, characterized by different Zak phases of the three bands. Our results provide a useful theoretical framework for interpreting existing experiments and serve as a guide for future experimental investigations of this system.

items.title: Entanglement and information dynamics in charged dual-unitary circuits with impurities
items.summary: Local parts of a closed, non-equilibrium quantum many-body system can reach stationarity through the buildup of entanglement between different regions. In this paper we investigate how this process is affected by the presence of a quantum impurity that breaks a global symmetry of the bulk. In particular, we study a charged dual-unitary quantum circuit perturbed by a symmetry-breaking, non-dual-unitary gate acting on a spatially fixed pair of sites. In this setup we calculate the entanglement entropy for a subsystem that does not contain the impurity, as well as the mutual information and logarithmic negativity for a bipartite subsystem that straddles the impurity. We obtain exact results in the early time regime for these quantities from the dual unitarity of the bulk system. Beyond this regime, we compute the predictions of the quasiparticle and entanglement membrane pictures, supporting them with exact calculations obtained by taking the corresponding limits of the bulk entangling power. We find that the presence of a symmetry-breaking impurity can lead to a richer behaviour of quantum relaxation, including non-monotonic evolution of the entanglement entropy, a modification of the long-time steady state, and persistent subsystem mutual information and entanglement negativity. This behaviour is understood in terms of long-range correlations generated by scattering from the impurity, and facilitated by the ballistic propagation of the conserved charges.

items.title: High Entropy Oxides as Room Temperature Anderson Insulators with Colossal Soft Gaps
items.summary: The Anderson effect, arising from destructive quantum interference of electron wave packets in disordered potentials, is usually observed at cryogenic temperatures and typically arises from extrinsic defects in conventional materials such as phosphorus dopants in silicon or oxygen vacancies in transition metal oxides. Here we demonstrate that a multication lattice of transition metals in a high-entropy oxide (HEO) natively establishes an interacting Anderson insulator that extends up to $500\,\mathrm{K}$. By controlling the population of transition metal cations in $\mathrm{La}_{0.7}\mathrm{Sr}_{0.3}\mathrm{Mn}_{1-x}(\mathrm{Cr},\mathrm{Fe},\mathrm{Co},\mathrm{Ni})_{x/4}\mathrm{O}_3$ (LS5B), we tune the system from the prototypical correlated metal $\mathrm{La}_{0.7}\mathrm{Sr}_{0.3}\mathrm{Mn}\mathrm{O}_3$ at $x=0.00$ to a localized insulator at $x=0.80$, where the disorder length contracts to near the unit cell (3.85 $\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$) and drives the electron mean free path to the Ioffe-Regel limit. Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) reveals the systematic localization of itinerant $d$-quasiparticle states at the Fermi level, consistent with the emergence of a soft Coulomb gap, while the underlying band structure and symmetry are preserved. Transport reveals Efros-Shklovskii variable-range hopping governed by a colossal soft gap with characteristic temperature $T_{\mathrm{ES}}>50{,}000\,\mathrm{K}$ and screened Coulomb interaction strengths as high as 1.6 eV. Together, multiple lines of evidence indicate that interacting Anderson behavior is a native characteristic that survives to temperatures as high as $500\,\mathrm{K}$ in high-entropy materials.

items.title: Validating Graph Neural Network Feature Attribution Through Local Perturbations: A Study on CoMoFeNiCu Decomposition Enthalpy
items.summary: Graph neural networks (GNNs) show promise for predicting materials properties, but interpretability remains a challenge, particularly understanding whether attributed feature importance reflects physical reality or statistical artifacts. Here, we present a methods validation study that deliberately overfits a physics-aware GNN ensemble to probe the robustness of feature-ranking approaches. Using the CoMoFeNiCu high-entropy alloy system with three stoichiometries, we train GNNs to predict decomposition enthalpies from DFT-calculated structures while explicitly constraining output weights to encode feature importance. By design, our dataset is limited (approximately 900 binary and 4,500 ternary decomposition pathways) to control compositional complexity and enable precise interrogation of local chemistry effects. We validate that feature rankings capture meaningful local-environment information through a series of atomic swap perturbations: perturbing individual atomic sites and re-ranking features reveals spatial decay consistent with the GNN's interaction cutoff, confirming that weights encode neighbor-shell effects rather than global stoichiometric artifacts alone. Results demonstrate that feature attribution methods can remain physically interpretable even under overfitting, provided validation is rigorous. This work establishes a foundation for trustworthy interpretability in materials GNNs and sets the stage for scaling to multiple chemistries and testing generalization across compositional spaces.

items.title: Transfer-Matrix Calculus for Infinite Matrix Product States
items.summary: Long-range interactions, from the Coulomb repulsion between electrons to the power-law interactions of trapped ions and Rydberg atoms, are widespread in quantum many-body physics. For infinite systems, however, MPS algorithms, the standard classical reference in one dimension, conventionally rely on a computational compromise: replacing these interactions by fitted sums of exponentials. We develop transfer-matrix calculus (TMC), a unified framework for deriving infinite-MPS algorithms. In TMC, an interaction is written as a function of the transfer matrix, and one set of contraction rules then yields the effective Hamiltonians of DMRG and VUMPS, the tangent-space excitation action, and the energy variance, without an MPO. Long-range interactions thus enter with their prescribed distance dependence. For the half-filled lattice Coulomb chain with a $1/d$ interaction of strength $V$, theory predicts CDW order for all $V>0$, but at weak coupling this order is too weak for earlier numerics to resolve. Using TMC, we obtain infinite-MPS ground states at $V=2$ directly in the thermodynamic limit, with an energy variance per site of $2\times10^{-10}$. Our data, extrapolated to zero energy variance, indicate a small nonzero CDW amplitude, $m_0=0.002213(14)$, consistent with this prediction. The complete $V=2$ optimization workflow across the full series of bond dimensions takes less than a day on a single AMD MI250X GPU die. For an exactly solvable long-range hopping model, TMC reproduces the nonanalytic $|k|$ cusp of the one-particle dispersion that any fixed finite sum of decaying exponentials rounds off. We also use TMC to optimize first-quantized MPS directly in the thermodynamic limit. For half-filled free fermions, our entanglement entropy data show scaling consistent with central charge $c=1$ over the studied bond dimensions, as for second-quantized MPS.

items.title: Graph diffusion transformer for interpretable generation and inverse design of disordered atomic structures
items.summary: Atomic disorder offers a potent degree of freedom to tailor material properties, yet the resulting vast configuration space obscures structure-property relations and hinders rational inverse design. Here we introduce Graph Amorphous Diffusion Transformer (GaDiT), a generative model that combines dynamic periodic graphs, masked conditioning and an interval-weighted training-noise distribution. GaDiT generates high-quality disordered structures while accelerating sampling by two orders of magnitude compared with existing corrector-based approaches, as demonstrated across two-dimensional amorphous carbon and three-dimensional amorphous silicon and silica. Moreover, GaDiT supports conditional generation under single or combined structural features, physical properties and preparation conditions in a unified model, and enables inverse design that expands accessible structure-property ranges beyond the training distribution. To interpret these structures and the trained network, we propose a conditioned atomic response mapping analysis, revealing both the global structural descriptors and the local atomic environments that govern target properties. Overall, GaDiT establishes a general framework for interpretable generation, inverse design and structure-property discovery for disordered atomic structures.

items.title: Emergent intercellular contact-force networks shaped by deformability
items.summary: We present a numerical study of contact-force organization in dense assemblies of active, deformable cells. Using the Fourier Contour Cell model, which enables efficient simulation of large cell deformations, we investigate how cell deformability and active motility shape spatial organization of intercellular forces. We find that, in the soft liquid regime at intermediate self-propulsion strength, the contact-force distribution becomes bimodal, reflecting the emergence of a distinct population of weak interactions. Persistent-homology analysis further reveals a characteristic force-network structure in which weak tip-tip interactions are enclosed by loops of strong side-side interactions. Simulations with elongated but non-deformable cells demonstrate that both the bimodal force distribution and the associated network motif require cell deformability rather than elongated cell shape per se. Furthermore, introducing a curvature constraint shows that local cell curvature regulates the strength of weak tip-tip interactions. Together, these results demonstrate that cell deformability and local geometric constraints can organize force transmission across dense active cellular assemblies.

items.title: Testing correlated spin--orbit multiplets beyond excitation centroids
items.summary: Matching an excitation centroid does not establish the resolved structure of a correlated spin--orbit multiplet. Across eight embedded iridium and osmium compounds, ligand-active XMS-CASPT2 places the K$_2$OsCl$_6$ centroid within 0.5~meV of a RIXS maximum while splitting its nearly degenerate reference triplet by 2.54~meV, and matched OpenMolcas 26.10 controls retain the bare-anion sensitivities. Independent BAGEL calculations isolate contraction dependence in a three-state spin-free model: on the same reference, replacing SS--SR with MS--MR reduces the symmetry-defined E-block splitting from 0.448~meV to $4.67\times10^{-5}$~meV. Native reconstruction, reference symmetry, representation invariance, sensitivity controls and comparison with fitted spectral features or magnetic response provide an ordered validation procedure whose tests constrain different properties of the Hamiltonian.

items.title: Macroscopic Nuclear Resonance Energy Transfer Mediated by Coherent Magnons
items.summary: Phonon-mediated nuclear Resonance Energy Transfer (RET) in metal deuterides is severely constrained by inertial rest-mass dilution, lattice fracture limits, and thermal nuclear spin cancellation. Extending the generalized nuclear Dicke model to Ferromagnetic Resonance (FMR) magnons eliminates mass dilution via hyperfine-amplified M1 coupling while unlocking relativistic Dirac M2 coupling via Overhauser spin polarization. We derive a Suhl-clamped FMR scaling law predicting 14.2 MeV (Pd-106) and 11.4 MeV (Ni-58) breakup neutrons, 19.9 MeV alpha particles, and reconciled sub-keV fusion anomalies.

items.title: Phase-resolved spin-orbit exciton transfer with dressed quantum encodings
items.summary: A quantum simulation of a material runs on a register much smaller than the electronic problem behind it, and the map between the two decides what a measured correlation means. We study this map for spin--orbit exciton transfer across an Ir--Ir bond of a LiIrF$_6$-derived model. Exact references show that a bare product-state encoding has an amplitude floor above a 0.02 state tolerance at sampled times, whereas a polar-dressed encoding lowers the ten-window projected error from 0.320 to $3.54\times10^{-4}$. Three-CZ axial and two-CZ transverse circuits, run on IBM Kingston in eight acquisitions with 1.6 million shots, resolve population transfer together with both quadratures of the intersite coherence. Raw half-transfer Bell-projector scores reach 0.935 in two independent acquisitions, and on a second bond a coherent arm with lower bound 0.871 is separated from a matched dephased control. Across 2,520 model points, adaptive spectral encodings meet fixed accuracy targets with explicit dimension costs.

items.title: Uniaxial strain induces $d$-wave phonon chirality in ferroelectric BaTiO$_3$
items.summary: Circularly dichroic resonant inelastic x-ray scattering has revealed electrically switchable $g$-wave phonon chirality in freestanding BaTiO$_3$ membranes. Here, we show from first principles that uniaxial strain changes the angular class of this texture. Lowering $C_{4v}$ to $C_{2v}$ adds a $d$-wave helicity that is bilinear in the orthorhombic strain $η$ and the polarization, with nodal lines along the stress axis. For the 38~meV branches at $η=1\%$, we find that (i) along the diagonal, where the helicity vanishes by symmetry without strain, it reaches about 60\% of the unstrained maximum, and (ii) at the measured wave vectors off the mirror it is reduced by more than half. With PBEsol and PBE+D3 force constants, the $d$-wave component grows linearly in $η$ and equals the $g$-wave one at $η^*\approx1.3\text{--}1.4\%$. Resolved by branch, the response of strain-split $E$ doublets is non-analytic in $η$, as captured by a two-band model. Strain therefore provides a second knob, besides the electric field, that controls the symmetry and the sign of phonon chirality in ferroelectric membranes.

items.title: A fast and rigorous numerical tool to measure length-scale artifacts in molecular simulations
items.summary: The two-sided Bogoliubov inequality for classical and quantum many-body systems is a theorem that provides rigorous bounds on the free-energy cost of partitioning a given system into two or more independent subsystems. This theorem motivates the definition of a quality factor which directly quantifies the degree of statistical-mechanical consistency achieved by a given simulation box size. A major technical merit of the theorem is that, for systems with two-body interactions and a known radial distribution function, the quality factor can be computed by evaluating just three six-dimensional integrals. We present a numerical algorithm for computing the quality factor and demonstrate its consistency with respect to results in the literature obtained from simulations performed at different box sizes.

items.title: Topological Hybridization Gaps from Molecular Orbitals Coupled to Dirac Fermions
items.summary: A magnetically gapped topological-insulator surface carries a half-quantized Hall response. We show that hybridizing the surface Dirac fermions with a flat band of chiral orbitals adds an integer to it: spin-momentum locking forces the hybridization to wind around the band-crossing ring, opening a topological gap. For orbitals with total angular momentum $j$, rotational symmetry fixes the surface Hall conductivity to $je^2/h$, with the sign set by the Dirac branch crossed and independent of the sign of the Dirac mass. The result survives crystal-field quenching of the orbital moment, with the winding then set by interference between hybridization pathways. First-principles calculations for a monolayer of nitric oxide adsorbed on Bi$_2$Se$_3$ predict a $\sim 20$ meV hybridization gap and an intrinsic surface Hall conductivity of $\frac{3}{2}e^2/h$, identifying molecular orbital angular momentum as a handle on surface topology.

items.title: Edge spin generalization for quantum Hall Laughlin droplets with elliptic shapes
items.summary: It is known that quasiparticles in the bulk of quantum Hall systems possess an emergent spin, which satisfies a spin-statistics relation. Recent results show that this spin can fractionalize: a quasiparticle spin in the bulk induces an opposite edge spin on the boundary. So far, the edge spin has only been studied in the simplest possible geometries, where the boundary is either circular or straight, without considering that a generic confining potential could give the droplet a non-symmetric shape. Yet, the value of the edge spin is not dictated by symmetry, but by topology: it is expected that the specific shape of the edge should not matter. In this work, we therefore generalize the edge spin to elliptically shaped droplets. We consider two different generalizations of the edge spin and test them on a family of elliptic Laughlin states introduced in the present work. The first, most straightforward, generalization is based on the properties of the single-particle orbitals for the elliptic confining potential. We show that this proposal applies to non-interacting states. The second proposal is based on the emergent properties of the quantum fluid. We show that this proposal also applies to interacting states, making it the suitable definition of the edge spin in the elliptic case. Our work demonstrates that it is possible to define an edge spin for Laughlin fluids with a non-trivial shape.

items.title: Guerra Interpolation and Optimal Transport: Kantorovich Bounds, Brenier Maps and the Replicon
items.summary: Since Guerra's work, mean-field spin glasses have been studied through Hamilton--Jacobi equations. Here, using the Curie--Weiss and the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick models as prototypical examples, we show that his celebrated interpolation method is itself an optimal transport computation. After a linear change of variables the finite-$N$ pressure becomes an action $u$ with $\partial_t u = -A/2$ and $\partial_x u = -B$, where $B^2 \le A$, so $u$ is a classical subsolution of $\partial_t u+\frac12(\partial_x u)^2 \le 0$. Integrating along a straight segment gives Guerra's sum rule, and dropping its remainder makes $u(0,\cdot)$ and $u(t,\cdot)$ an admissible pair for the dual Kantorovich problem with quadratic cost. For the Curie--Weiss model and $t > 0$, $T_t(y) = y-t\tanh y$ is an optimal transport map from every source with finite first moment if and only if $t \le 1$, and the Kantorovich potentials are the limiting pressures. For the replica-symmetric Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model, the cavity map is injective on the physical half-line and the curvature of its Brenier potential is the longitudinal eigenvalue, which exceeds the replicon eigenvalue $Λ_{\mathrm{AT}}$: transport of Dirac masses does not detect the de Almeida--Thouless line. The replicon appears along the $\mathcal{W}_2$ geodesic that splits a Dirac mass into two atoms, as the second variation of a second-order surrogate of the two-atom Parisi functional. From a Dirac initial datum, Guerra's $K$-step bound takes Hopf--Lax form, and the Parisi formula becomes a Hopf--Lax formula over atomic measures. With a $\mathcal{W}_1$-Lipschitz bound for its initial datum, proved by comparing Cole--Hopf layers, we let $K\to\infty$ and recover at Dirac data the Hopf--Lax form of the Parisi formula due to Mourrat and to Mourrat and Panchenko, with a rate for equal-mass approximations.

items.title: Adjoint-State Identifiability of Piezo-Tunable Valley Splitting in 2D Magnetic Heterostructures
items.summary: Mechanical strain has been proposed to dynamically tune proximity-induced valley splitting in 2D magnetic heterostructures for solid-state information processing. While first-principles studies routinely predict strain-modulated valley splittings at the atomic scale, they rarely address whether the coupling parameter can be extracted from a macroscopic transport measurement against realistic device noise. This paper develops a classical, partial differential equation-constrained multiscale inverse framework to quantify the device-level identifiability of the exchange-strain coupling from a transverse Hall voltage in a molybdenum disulfide and chromium tribromide heterostructure. Structural relaxation confirms a chiral $C_3$ point-group symmetry of the Hollow-stacked structure, and Neumann's principle reduces the coupling tensor to a single scalar $η$. Dispersion-corrected density functional theory gives a zero-strain splitting of -0.45 meV and bounds the coupling to $|η| \lesssim 2$ meV at small tensile strain while leaving its sign open, motivating the transport analysis. For an example coupling of $|η| = 0.56$ meV, where an actuator strain trace of $3.5 \times 10^{-4}$ shifts the valley splitting by only 0.2 $μ$eV, operation at 10 K below the Curie temperature of CrBr$_3$ makes the coupling statistically resolvable from 5.6 to 3,704 V/cm. Even in a demanding stress test recovering $η$ jointly with the zero-strain splitting, an uncalibrated Hall gain, and an unknown intervalley scattering time, the window spans 25 to 3,704 V/cm and the Cramér-Rao bound at the 10% velocity-saturation limit reaches 13.6 $μ$eV, 21 times below the resolution criterion. Since this window covers the full operational bias range of 2D field-effect transistors, from low-power linear readout to high-field drive, this framework serves as a pre-fabrication diagnostic for valleytronic devices.

items.title: Surface Roughness and Filler Restructuring in Magneto-Active Elastomers: Magnetically Hard versus Magnetically Soft Particles
items.summary: In magneto-active elastomers (MAEs), a magnetic field reshapes the surface and with it adhesion, friction and wetting. Most use magnetically soft carbonyl iron, whose restructuring has lacked a particle-resolved description. We put forward a molecular dynamics model with magnetizable particles and compare thin layers of hard and soft fillers. Both converge to the same high-field state: a labyrinth of bundled field-aligned chains roughening the surface by about one particle diameter. Hard fillers break and rotate in-plane chains above a threshold field, roughening the surface abruptly. Soft fillers build chains particle by particle, roughening it continuously. The model reproduces the magnetization of carbonyl iron MAEs above about 250 mT and the magnitude of their roughness. Measured roughness varies linearly with inverse zero-field Young's modulus: matrix stiffness, not particle number, controls it. At equal saturation magnetization, filler type sets not how rough the surface becomes, but whether it roughens abruptly or continuously.

items.title: Catenaries in viscous fluid
items.summary: This work explores a simple model of a slender, flexible structure in a uniform flow, providing analytical solutions for the translating, axially flowing equilibria of strings subjected to a uniform body force and drag forces linear in the velocities. The classical catenaries are extended to a five-parameter family of curves. A sixth parameter affects the tension in the curves. Generic configurations are planar, represented by a single first order equation for the tangential angle. The effects of varying parameters on representative shapes, orbits in angle-curvature space, and stress distributions are shown. As limiting cases, the solutions include configurations corresponding to "lariat chains" and the towing, reeling, and sedimentation of flexible cables in a highly viscous fluid. Regions of parameter space corresponding to infinitely long, semi-infinite, and finite length curves are delineated. Almost all curves subtend an angle less than $π$ radians, but curious special cases with doubled or infinite range occur on the borders between regions. Separate transitions in the tension behavior, and counterintuitive results regarding finite towing tensions for infinitely long cables, are presented. Several physically inspired boundary value problems are solved and discussed.

items.title: Frustrated Interlayer Coupling Creates a Higher-Order Helical Superstructure in a Twist-Bend Smectic Phase
items.summary: Bent liquid-crystalline dimers provide a model system for studying the spontaneous emergence of chirality from achiral molecules. Depending on terminal-chain length, these materials exhibit a competition between heliconical, synclinic, and anticlinic packing tendencies in tilted smectic phases. In short homologues, the tendency to form twist-bend phases dominates, leading to two distinct helical phases: the SmCTB-SH phase, with a helical periodicity of four molecular lengths, and at lower temperatures, a double helical structure - the SmCTB-DH phase, with progressive rotation of the four-layer unit. With increasing terminal chain length, this twist-bend tendency is gradually suppressed, favoring phases with simple synclinic and anticlinic tilt arrangement in successive layers. Remarkably, in the regime where these tendencies become comparable, a new modulated smectic phase, SmCTB-mod develops; a double helical structure in which the internal four-layer unit undergoes a periodic modulation. This additional level of structural organization provides a means of accommodating competing heliconical and synclinic/anticlinic tendencies and produces a characteristic splitting of the resonant x-ray diffraction peaks into four signals symmetrically located around a signal of four-layer periodicity. These results reveal how bent dimers resolve local-packing-mode frustration through complex spontaneous hierarchical structural organization.

items.title: Symmetry induced spin splitting of topological surface states at equal carrier density
items.summary: Surface states are among the most striking consequences of band inversion in topological materials. In magnetotransport of three-dimensional topological insulators, the typical signature of surface state transport is a quantized Hall conductance with nontrivial sequences of integer filling factors, varying with the total carrier density. For two independent Dirac carriers, one expects Hall plateaus only at odd-integer filling factors. In this work, we report the observation of symmetry induced spin splitting in magnetotransport experiments on a dual-gate three-dimensional topological insulator device based on HgTe. In the topological surface state regime, we observe Hall plateaus at both odd and even integers when we gate the device symmetrically, i.e., with equal density at the top and bottom. This phenomenon originates in structural inversion symmetry, which remarkably induces a spin splitting and forces the eigenstates to be symmetric and antisymmetric linear combinations of the top and bottom surface states. This is in contrast with two-dimensional systems, where spin splitting is caused by absence of inversion symmetry. We interpret the experimental observations with a perturbative model using isoparity eigenstates, the conserved quantum number associated with structural inversion. The result demonstrates that the picture where the top and bottom states are treated as independent Dirac carriers is not valid when the carrier density is symmetric.

items.title: Delay-induced current reversal in traveling activity waves
items.summary: Self-propelled particles that regulate their speed based on a response to a local activity source can move with or against a traveling wave of that source depending on their response time. Silica-titania Janus microswimmers, whose UV-controlled speed relaxes with a delay intrinsic to the titania photoconductivity adaptation, carry two independent memory channels: the familiar directional memory dictated by persistent active Brownian motion, and a distinct memory from the speed adaptation. Combining experiments, Langevin simulations, and a moment expansion of the corresponding Fokker-Planck equation, we show that this delayed response to speed adaptation reshapes transport under traveling UV-illumination waves and can even reverse it relative to the direction set by orientational memory alone. In particular, we observe that delay promotes transport in the direction opposite to the traveling activity waves, where, beyond a critical value, the particle current reverses with respect to the wave propagation direction. Crucially, this behavior requires an asymmetric response to the speed adaptation, with an instantaneous rise but a delayed fall upon exposure to time-varying UV light. Theory further shows that this phenomenology is specific to the response asymmetry rather than to the mere presence of a delay, i.e. reversing the asymmetry reverses the effect of the delay on the particle current relative to the wave. We thus establish propulsion-delay asymmetry as a control parameter for directed transport of responsive active particles in traveling activity landscapes.

items.title: Exact anomalous current fluctuations in the strong-anisotropy limit of the XXZ chain
items.summary: We study spin-current fluctuations of the folded XXZ chain, which describes the strong-anisotropy limit of the XXZ chain. We obtain an exact expression for the moment-generating function of the time-integrated spin current at infinite temperature. A long-time asymptotic analysis establishes that the rescaled time-integrated current converges to a non-Gaussian distribution described by the M-Wright function. The derivation relies on a nonlocal map to the one-dimensional t-0 model and its exact spin-charge separation. By extending this approach, we also show that the dynamical correlation function of the spins summed over two adjacent sites exhibits a diffusive Gaussian profile at long times.

items.title: Bond Anharmonicity in a Caged Molecule Probed by Vibronic Core Spectroscopy
items.summary: X-ray absorption spectroscopy and resonant inelastic X-ray scattering at the nitrogen K-edge show that the N$\equiv$N bond in N$_2$@C$_{60}$ is substantially more anharmonic than in free N$_2$, with the ground-state ($X^1Σ_g^+$) anharmonic constant $\hbarω_e x_e$ a factor of two larger ($3.8\pm0.3$~meV versus $\sim 1.8$~meV) despite an essentially unchanged harmonic frequency. The same enhancement is found across all three vibronic potentials accessible to the experiment---the electronic ground state, the core-excited intermediate state, and the spectator-decay final state---pointing to a common origin rather than an effect specific to one electronic configuration. High-level coupled-cluster calculations of the N$_2$@C$_{60}$ potential energy surface, however, find no significant change in anharmonicity upon encapsulation, ruling out a simple static distortion of the N$\equiv$N bonding potential by the fullerene cage. We propose instead that the dramatic increase in $\hbarω_e x_e$ above the gas-phase value -- which, taken literally, would imply an unphysical halving of the N$_2$ dissociation energy - reflects the breakdown of the single-molecule Morse description, as previously invoked to explain anomalous anharmonicities in N$_2$ clusters, and supported by the observation of shifts in the fullerene host's Raman modes.

items.title: Scalable topological quantum computing based on Sine-Cosine chain models
items.summary: We propose a scalable framework for quantum information processing based on Matryoshka-type sine-cosine chains, a hierarchy of one-dimensional chiral-symmetric lattices obtained by repeated ($P$ times) square-root construction starting from the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain. A chain of order $P$ can host $2^{P+2}-2$ protected edge states, so a single physical device can encode a qudit of equivalent dimension (or, equivalently, several independent qubits) instead of one qubit per device. We show that (i) the adiabatic defect-transfer step underlying SSH-based topological gates carries over unchanged to the Matryoshka chain, transferring the full set of defect states simultaneously; (ii) a Y-junction braiding protocol then composes single-qudit gate operations in all energy sectors at once, increasing the operation density per physical device; and (iii) the same edge states provide a quantum memory whose capacity scales exponentially with the chain order at fixed physical length. Numerical fidelity analysis under on-site, hopping, and correlated angle disorder shows partial, chiral-symmetry-protected robustness.

items.title: Quantized resistance limitations for graphene p-n junction devices
items.summary: Developing high-resistance quantized Hall resistance standards requires accessing values beyond the robust value seen in epitaxial graphene (R_{\mathrm{H}}=\ \frac{1}{2}\frac{h}{e^{2}}). This study evaluates the available parameter space of the coefficient of effective resistance across various epitaxial graphene p-n junction topologies, including rectangular, Corbino, and triangular layouts. Because mapping desired resistances to device configurations is mathematically degenerate, an automated Landauer-Büttiker Python solver was developed for all three topologies and was validated by cryogenic multi-terminal transport measurements and LTspice simulations. By analyzing the Shannon entropy of available states, it is found that rectangular checkerboards maximize topological complexity and tunable outputs, whereas Corbino geometries exhibit highly constrained resistance availabilities.

items.title: Correlation functions of the Lieb--Liniger Bose gas in equilibrium states: a microscopic approach to space-time asymptotics
items.summary: We develop an approximation-free approach to the analysis of form-factor series for the correlation functions of quantum integrable models in the thermodynamic limit and in equilibrium states described by a class of stationary density matrices. This allows us to obtain the long-time, large-distance asymptotics of the correlation functions in thermal equilibrium and in stationary states after a quench, including such states that can be described by generalized Gibbs ensembles. Our approach will be exemplified with the Lieb--Liniger Bose gas or non-linear Schrödinger model. It applies to the correlation functions of all local operators. For the two-point functions of particle-density or particle-current density operators our findings confirm the phenomenological predictions based on generalised hydrodynamics. We extract as well the long-time, large-distance asymptotics of a field- conjugated field correlation function. At present its behaviour is outside the reach of any heuristic method. It is governed by a novel non-linear integral equation that depends on space and time.

items.title: CGTransformer: A Topology-Aware Autoregressive Framework for Crystal Generation and Inverse Design
items.summary: Autoregressive language models offer a unified route to crystal generation and inverse design, but their performance depends on how periodic structures are serialized. Symmetry equivalent and closely related crystals can receive different atomic orders under coordinate-based serialization, introducing variability unrelated to their structural connectivity. Here, we present CGTransformer (Crystal Graph Transformer), an autoregressive generative framework that addresses this challenge via a graph-embedded sorting strategy. Using quotientgraph topology and barycentric embeddings, Element Symmetry Graph (ESG) converts periodic crystal networks into topology-guided one-dimensional sequences that retain key local and symmetry-related structural information. CGTransformer achieves high generation validity and the highest single shot crystal structure prediction (CSP) match rate among the compared MP-20 baselines (63.24%), while same backbone comparisons show improved structure recovery over coordinate-based ordering. Furthermore, we demonstrate property-conditioned inverse design for wide-bandgap semiconductors, where ESG achieves a much higher stable, unique and novel (S.U.N.) rate and stronger target-property alignment than the coordinate-based baseline. These results establish topology-guided sequence construction as an effective route to improving crystal generation and property-directed design at fixed model capacity.

items.title: A Tissue Vertex Model grounded in Continuum Mechanics
items.summary: Practical modeling of disordered single-layer confluent tissues has relied heavily on the two-dimensional standard vertex model (SVM), which simplifies cell elasticity using an energy functional determined by quadratic dependence of cell area and perimeter values. Realistically, even a coarse-grained cell interior consists of effective continuum materials representing cytoplasm and peripheral cortex, with elastic energy depending on stress and strain fields. It is shown that this energy is analytically tractable for polygonal cell shapes, that its area dependence can be eliminated, that it correlates well with cell perimeter length, and that the perimeter dependence of the correlation is not quadratic. This results in a revised vertex model derived from continuum elasticity whose parameters are predicted from tissue material properties and whose resultant forces are far less strain-dependent than in the SVM.

items.title: Thermally Hysteretic Room-Temperature Nonlinear Hall Effect in Bulk EuTe4
items.summary: The nonlinear Hall effect (NLHE) is a novel transport phenomena and shows great potential applications of future electronics. However, the realization of a giant and tunable NLHE in bulk materials at room temperature remains elusive. Here, we report a NLHE in bulk EuTe4 single crystals, which persists up to 400 K and exhibits pronounced thermal hysteresis behaviors. The ratio of nonlinear Hall voltages during warming and cooling processes is about 4.7 at 340 K. Such phenomena could be related to the inversion-symmetry-broken charge density wave state in EuTe4. These findings demonstrate bulk EuTe$_4$ as a promising platform for tunable nonlinear electronic devices at room temperature.

items.title: Digitally-alloyed magnetic topological insulator nanostructures grown via stencil mask molecular beam epitaxy
items.summary: Magnetic topological insulator nanostructures are a promising platform for the realization of fault-tolerant quantum computation. For this, such nanostructures need to be embedded into the necessary superconducting architectures. In this study, we demonstrate a method for the growth of magnetic topological insulator nanostructures via molecular beam epitaxy, utilising digital alloying and defining their shapes in-situ by stencil mask technology. Cr-doped (Bi$_y$Sb$_{1-y}$)$_2$Te$_3$ micro- and nanometer-sized Hall bars are fabricated and the magneto-transport properties for various Cr doping amounts and different Hall bar dimensions are investigated at low temperatures. We find indications that the Fermi energy is located inside the bulk band gap, while disorder and charge puddles affect the transport behaviour. Furthermore, we investigate the magnetic properties and discuss the transition from ferromagnetic to paramagnetic behaviour.

items.title: Observing Enhanced Entanglement in an Ising Quantum Register Beyond Weak Measurement
items.summary: Measurements often yield a disentangled quantum state which is the most probable measurement outcome while the measurement outcomes with enhanced entanglement could be exponentially less probable or absent. Higher probability in measurement outcomes with enhanced entanglement is virtue in experimental observation of enhance entanglement in post-selected or Born-rule measurements with less resources in noisy quantum devices. We develop a periodic measurement sampling(PMS) protocol in the framework of uniform matrix product states. Using PMS, we identify a peak enhancement of entanglement in a uniform post-measurement state whose probabilistic outcome can be maximized by optimizing a measurement super-cell. A measurement super-cell is the smallest repeating building block of qubits defined by the measurement density, external field strength and exchange interactions between quantum register and ancilla qubits. The above prediction based on a classical description of the many-body quantum state is demonstrated in a quantum computing experiment in a loop of quantum register qubits with Ising interactions in the presence of transverse magnetic field. Further, we show the scalability of predictions of the periodic measurement sampling protocol in the thermodynamic limit to finite size systems. Especially, we present a rescaling ansatz which would enable predicting the possibility of observing enhanced entanglement in finite size systems.

items.title: SmoQyElPhQMC.jl: An open-source Julia package for efficient and scalable quantum Monte Carlo simulations of electron-phonon coupled models
items.summary: We introduce version 1.0 of the SmoQyElPhQMC.jl package, an open-source Julia code for performing scalable quantum Monte Carlo simulations of electron-phonon coupled model Hamiltonians. SmoQyElPhQMC.jl is built upon the SmoQyDQMC.jl codebase and implements improved versions of the algorithms presented in [B. Cohen-Stead \textit{et al}., Phys. Rev. E 105, 065302 (2022)] to enable (near-linear) scalable simulations of a broad class of uncorrelated $e$-ph models both in system size and inverse temperature. By extending the functionality of the flexible scripting interface introduced in SmoQyDQMC.jl, the SmoQyElPhQMC.jl package continues to allow users to adapt it to different workflows and interface with other software packages in the Julia ecosystem. The code for this package can be downloaded from our GitHub repository at https://github.com/SmoQySuite/SmoQyElPhQMC.jl or installed using the Julia package manager. The online documentation, including examples, can be obtained from our documentation page at https://smoqysuite.github.io/SmoQyElPhQMC.jl/stable/.

items.title: Mechanical acclimation of bacterial growth and division across generations
items.summary: Bacteria frequently encounter mechanical confinement in natural and engineered environments, yet how an abrupt change in mechanical conditions reorganizes growth and division across generations remains poorly understood. Using single-cell time-lapse microscopy, we tracked Escherichia coli across generations following transfer from liquid culture to glass-attached or glass-gel-confined conditions. This mechanical confinement causes an immediate reduction in elongation rate, followed by a multi-generational mechanical acclimation process whose dynamics depend systematically on confinement strength. During this relaxation, division behavior becomes more heterogeneous and cells temporarily depart from canonical adder-like size regulation, exhibiting timer-like correlation signatures. Using a stochastic cell-cycle model that resolves the generation-dependent correlation signatures of different size-control strategies, we show that changes in elongation rate alone cannot account for the observed transition in growth-division coordination. Despite this transient reorganization, the birth-size distribution remains bounded and largely preserves its shape throughout acclimation. Notably, adder-like regulation is restored before the elongation rate fully recovers, revealing distinct relaxation timescales for growth and size-control dynamics. These results establish bacterial size control under mechanical confinement as a dynamical nonequilibrium process in which growth and division can transiently reorganize while global size homeostasis is maintained.

items.title: Real-Space-RG for the drawups and drawdowns of run-and-tumble trajectories: universality classes for models with space-dependent velocities and switching rates
items.summary: For one-dimensional run-and-tumble processes with the two velocities $v_{\pm}(x)$ and the two switching rates $γ_{\pm}(x)$, a given stochastic trajectory is an alternating sequence of local minima and local maxima corresponding to the switching events between the ballistic motions with velocities $v_{\pm}(x) $ in the two directions. The renormalized trajectory at scale $Γ$ is obtained by keeping only the alternating sequence of local minima and local maxima that are separated by drawups and drawdowns of amplitude bigger than $Γ$. Its statistical properties can be analyzed via the generalization of the previous work arxiv:2611.04853 concerning diffusion processes involving arbitrary diffusion coefficients $D(x)$ and Ito forces $F_I(x)$. The main result is that the scale function $s(x)$ of diffusion processes that depends only on the ratio $\frac{F_I(x)}{D(x) } $ is replaced by a pair of scale functions $s_{\pm}(x)$ that depend only on the two ratios $\frac{γ_+( x ) }{v_+( x )}$ and $\frac{γ_-( x ) }{v_-( x )}$. This pair of scale functions $s_{\pm}(x)$ govern the exit probabilities from an interval and determine the universality classes of the renormalized trajectories: all run-and-tumble processes with the same two ratios $\frac{γ_+( x ) }{v_+( x )}$ and $\frac{γ_-( x ) }{v_-( x )}$ share the same statistics of renormalized trajectories. This general framework is illustrated with examples that are compared to their diffusive counterparts : uniform symmetric and asymmetric processes on the whole line $x \in]-\infty,+\infty[$, geometric process on the half-line $x \in]0,+\infty[$, and an exponential functional of the telegraph process with a normalizable steady state.

items.title: Quantum limits on squeezing
items.summary: In our work, we show how, for a network of bosonic modes, canonical commutation relations constrain the coefficients relating input and internal modes. Based on these constraints, we derive a lower bound on the total steady-state squeezing achievable in reservoir-engineered (dissipative) squeezing schemes, quantified by the sum of mode-optimal quadrature variances each normalized to its corresponding input variance. The bound on this normalized sum follows solely from canonical commutation relations and stability, and is saturated in the strong-coupling limit at unity. Furthermore, we show that adding independent parametric driving terms for each mode changes the quantum noise--gain balance and yields, for the same normalized mode-optimal sum, a distinct optimum bound, approaching 1/2. In addition, we show how these constraints allow us to reformulate the Duan inseparability criterion for a three-mode bosonic system in terms of a single parameter-dependent figure of merit. Our results apply directly to current electromechanical and nanomechanical experiments and indicate that the two-mode bounds can be experimentally approached even at room temperature.

items.title: Modification of optical properties in ultrathin ALD-grown NbN layers using oxygen plasma treatment
items.summary: NbN thin films with a nominal thickness of 10\,nm were grown by atomic layer deposition (ALD) on Al$_2$O$_3$-buffered Si substrates and treated with oxygen plasma for 0\,s (untreated), 20\,s, 40\,s, and 60\,s to investigate oxygen-induced changes in their optical properties. Spectroscopic ellipsometry (SE) measurements were performed before and after oxygen plasma treatment over the ultraviolet--visible--near-infrared (1.24--6.20\,eV) and infrared (0.041--0.827\,eV) spectral ranges. Film thickness determined by X-ray reflectivity (XRR) was used as a fixed parameter in the optical modeling to extract the dielectric function, optical constants, and effective free-carrier concentration. We observed the emergence of a distinct absorption feature near 4.9\,eV following oxygen plasma treatment, consistent with the oxidation of the NbN surface and the resulting change in its optical properties. Increasing the treatment time from 0 to 60\,s reduced the effective carrier concentration from $1.20 \times 10^{22}$ to $1.03 \times 10^{22}$\,cm$^{-3}$ and the effective carrier mobility from 2.44 to 2.27\,cm$^2$\,V$^{-1}$\,s$^{-1}$. The obtained results provide a basis for understanding the effects of oxygen plasma treatment on NbN thin films.

items.title: Thermalization Across Scales on a Digital Quantum Processor
items.summary: Thermalization of isolated quantum many-body systems normally unfolds via dynamical spreading of entanglement across progressively increasing spatial scales. The speed of this dynamical process, however, can be affected by the presence of local disorder. Here we study the crossover between slow and fast thermalization in a disordered two-dimensional Heisenberg Floquet model using digital quantum simulations with up to 100 superconducting qubits. Our experiment measures subsystem purities and $Z$-basis marginal collision entropies for patches of up to $3\times 3$ qubits. We resolve the onset of thermalization across scales by tracking each quantity's approach to its asymptotic value. In regimes where the system is moderately entangled, we validate our calibrated quantum simulations against state-of-the-art classical simulations. Near the crossover to fast thermalization, the classical methods no longer reliably converge due to volume-law growth of entanglement. By exploring this computationally hard regime, our work establishes a frontier of applications for digital quantum computers in probing complex many-body thermalization.

items.title: Dancing Tokens on the Vocabulary Network from LLM Generation
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) generate text one token at a time, yet how a particular generation relates to the geometry learned in pre-training remains unclear. The fundamental explainability of LLMs is elusive. Here, we build a similarity network from the input embeddings of six open LLMs and map generation onto it. The token-embedding network is scale-free while heavy-tailed, as are random embeddings with matched covariance, but far more fragmented. Distillation barely changes this topology because input embeddings are largely inherited. The knowledge space is thus deterministic from pre-training. Consecutive generated tokens are rarely graph neighbours and, in most models, no more often than in shuffled order, so generation is not a walk on the predefined network, although the tokens it visits are concentrated within it. Through the logit lens in a layer- wise manner, tokens settle late in depth in most models, and repetitive models remain confined to small domain-specific sub-graphs. These observables could serve as inference-time monitors of degeneration. We thus provide a fresh perspective on understanding LLM generation in the microscopic way from node or link prediction by graph learning.

items.title: Link invariants in nilpotent group gauge theories
items.summary: We consider 3-dimensional topological gauge theories with nilpotent gauge groups, both finite, that is Dijkgraaf-Witten theories, and continuous, that is Chern-Simons theories. Abelian topological quantum field theories are exactly those which do not detect the Borromean rings, and nilpotent gauge groups provide the natural next steps beyond the abelian case. We show that the untwisted Dijkgraaf-Witten theory with gauge group $G$ detects Brunnian links with up to $n+1$ components, but no Brunnian links with more components, if and only if $G$ is $n$-step nilpotent. Moreover, the expectation values of such links are determined by their Milnor invariants. We also study the properties of Chern-Simons theories with nilpotent Lie groups and draw parallels with those of the Dijkgraaf-Witten theories. Finally, we conjecture, using the Lazard correspondence, a relation between expectation values of line operators in the two types of theories, and test it in examples.

items.title: How Superradiance Survives Molecular Noise inside Virus Capsids
items.summary: Excited organic dyes chemically bound to an icosahedral virus shell can spontaneously synchronize and emit a superradiant burst of light. The mechanism that allows it to occur at room temperature, despite collisional dephasing and inhomogeneous broadening, is not understood. Few other known low-dimensional condensed matter systems exhibit room-temperature superradiance (SR). In the fluctuation-prone environment of molecular-based systems, electron--vibrational coupling has been proposed to play a central role. Here, we addressed experimentally the existence of underdamped virus capsid phonon-like modes and theoretically their involvement in the transition from uncorrelated to cooperative emission. We find that SR-active dye-labeled capsids exhibit underdamped low-frequency oscillations that modulate the dye excited-state response, and modeling shows how such capsid motion can promote the collective polarization required for superradiant emission.

items.title: A unified finite-site framework for scaffold-client biocondensation
items.summary: Client recruitment into biomolecular condensates does not determine how stronger binding changes the bulk free-energy advantage of demixing. Here, we use a unified finite-site thermodynamic framework to examine how scaffold-client interactions affect both the response of a fixed-composition mixture and the organization of its ternary phase diagram. The thermodynamic response to increasing client affinity is determined by the difference in heterotypic bonding between the complete equilibrium phase-separated sample and the corresponding homogeneous state. A finite region of the model exhibits positive scaffold-client concentration covariance but negative heterotypic bond contrast: stronger binding reduces the demixing advantage even when both species enrich in the dense phase. This reduction also occurs with independent scaffold self-association and client-binding site pools, without direct displacement of scaffold bonds. A negative response does not by itself imply condensate shrinkage or dissolution. Across composition space, the same finite binding constraints support scaffold-rich and heterotypic coexistence regimes with distinct bond populations. For divalent clients, these regimes can occupy disconnected regions of the phase diagram and reconnect upon increasing client affinity, depending on scaffold cohesion. Critical-point continuation identifies the folds and cusp organizing these changes, while client valence restricts the parameter range over which disconnected coexistence occurs. Explicit-particle Monte Carlo simulations reproduce the qualitative reentrant response and provide finite-size evidence for disconnected coexistence. These results provide a bond-resolved characterization of fixed-parent affinity response and a complementary description of coexistence under specified association constraints.

items.title: The Rise of Zirconium Metal-Organic Polyhedra
items.summary: Zirconium metal-organic polyhedra (Zr-MOPs) assembled from cyclopentadienyl (Cp)-capped Zr$_3$ clusters and carboxylate linkers form a structurally diverse family. Which MOP forms depends on the connectivity of the Zr$_3$ node, the geometry of the linker, and assembly conditions. This review classifies Zr-MOPs into edge- and face-directed tetrahedra, a cube, and cocoons according to the connectivity and geometry of their building blocks. From reported structures, we map which linkers give which MOPs and examine how the Zr$_3$ cluster precursor and the reaction conditions decide between the tetrahedron and the cocoon when one linker can give both. We describe how hydrogen bonding and ionic association organize the MOPs into reticular nets and porous salts in the crystal. Together, these comparisons relate cage geometry to node-linker connectivity and crystal packing to the geometry and distribution of external interaction sites, providing a structural basis for designing Zr-MOPs and their supramolecular assemblies.

items.title: Reconciling global and local spin models
items.summary: Magnetic interactions based on first-principles calculations can be casted either into global spin models, where the interactions are configuration-independent, or into local spin models, where the effective parameters depend explicitly on the underlying spin configuration. Although these two perspectives often yield seemingly inconsistent results, we demonstrate that they can be reconciled by restricting the analysis to transverse spin fluctuations. We develop a projection scheme that systematically removes spurious longitudinal contributions from local interaction matrices, thereby establishing a rigorous connection between the projected local interactions and the underlying global multispin Hamiltonian. Applying our approach to the prototype systems (i) a Cr trimer on Au(111) (ii) Fe and Cr dimers on Cu(001), we show that the projected local interaction parameters quantitatively reproduce those obtained from the global four-spin model. This work provides a unified framework to interpret local and global spin models on equal footing and resolves long-standing ambiguities in the identification of effective interactions such as the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI) in a non-collinear framework.

items.title: Facile On-Chip Growth and Spatially Selective Color Tuning of CsPbBr$_{3}$@TFA Nanoplatelets via Ion Engineering
items.summary: Metal halide perovskite (MHP) nanoplatelets are attractive for integrated optoelectronics because of their strong light-matter interactions and composition-tunable optical response. However, their high surface-to-volume ratio promotes surface defects and trap-assisted nonradiative recombination. In addition, their ionic nature facilitates rapid halide migration and limits selective composition tuning. Here, we combine in-synthesis (in situ) and post-synthesis ion engineering to suppress nonradiative recombination and enable selective on-chip color conversion.
