CsPbBr$_{3}$ nanoplatelets were grown directly on-chip via a solution process incorporating trifluoroacetate (TFA$^{-}$) pseudohalides. CsPbBr$_{3}$@TFA emits at 520 nm with a linewidth of 14.56 $\% \pm$ 0.5 nm and an average lifetime of 26.38 ns. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy shows that TFA$^{-}$ passivates uncoordinated Pb$^{2+}$ and suppresses metallic lead (Pb$^{0}$) formation. Spatially selective halide exchange was then achieved using a photolithographically patterned PMMA/Al$_{2}$O$_{3}$ mask to confine HCl vapor exposure. In the unmasked regions, the photoluminescence peak shifts from 520 nm to 413 nm, producing laterally defined green- and violet-emitting regions. The nanoplatelets were further integrated with graphene field-effect transistors, yielding responsivities of 2.5 x 10$^{5}$ A W$^{-1}$ at 450 nm and 1.9 x 10$^{5}$ A W$^{-1}$ at 370 nm, respectively. Our method enables scalable growth and selective color tuning of MHP nanoplatelets for on-chip optoelectronic integration.

items.title: Tunable coupling between valley and magnetic excitons in WS2/CrSBr heterostructures
items.summary: Interfacial coupling in van der Waals two-dimensional (2D) heterostructures offers an effective route to tailor the electronic, optical, and magnetic properties of materials. Versatile control and precise engineering of such interlayer interactions can be further achieved through external parameters, like electric field, magnetic field, optical excitation, as well as layer stacking geometries. Here, we examined the magneto-optical properties of 2D semiconductor heterostructures made of antiferromagnetic CrSBr and a monolayer WS2, both of which host intriguing excitonic properties. We identified a type-II band alignment between these two layers and the magnetic proximity effects from CrSBr, manifested by an enhanced Zeeman valley splitting in the WS2 layer. The interlayer charge transfer shows strong spin selectivity and is governed by the relative alignment between the valley-spin polarization of photoexcited carriers in WS2 and the magnetization in CrSBr, giving rise to spin-sensitive circularly polarized photoluminescence (PL) from WS2. Furthermore, the highly anisotropic electronic dispersion in CrSBr enables stacking-dependent control of interlayer interactions, as inferred from a twist-angle dependence of PL quenching. Our work establishes a highly tunable 2D system that integrates valleytronics and magnetic excitons through multiple coupling channels, opening up new opportunities in all-optical manipulation of spin and magnon states and for the development of flexible spin-optoelectronic devices.

items.title: Controlled Magnon Chirality and Its Reversal by Anisotropy in Altermagnetic FeF$_2$
items.summary: In altermagnets, the exchange symmetry of two mutually compensating magnetic sublattices permits spin-polarized electronic bands and chirality-split magnon bands. Because these effects have opposite signs in domains related by time reversal, magnetic-domain control is essential for their observation and utilization. Using half-polarized neutron diffraction, we demonstrate that we can control magnetic domain imbalance in a single crystal of FeF$_2$ by field cooling, and we relate this response to the established piezomagnetism in this material. Our half-polarized inelastic neutron scattering measurements directly resolve the altermagnetic splitting of chiral magnon bands. Strikingly, we observe a clear reversal of chirality near $\mathbf{Q}=(0.5,0.5,1)$, where the altermagnetic exchange splitting vanishes and no chirality is expected in a nonrelativistic exchange model. This reversal of the chirality is well explained by the presence of a transverse component of the single-ion anisotropy tensor, which rotates between Fe sublattices related by the crystal's altermagnetic $4_2$ screw symmetry. These results allow us to resolve fine features of the spin Hamiltonian for FeF$_2$ and show how symmetry-governed relativistic anisotropy can reshape altermagnetic spin dynamics, as well as providing an avenue for control of magnetic domains and the net chiral response.

items.title: Mapping the Phase Space of Cubic Chiral Semiconductors: High-Throughput Search,Stability, and Prototype Families
items.summary: Chiral crystals show unique electronic, magnetic, and optical characteristics that make them attractive for topological and spintronic applications. Nevertheless, the limited set of identified chiral semiconductors, especially those with cubic symmetry, has so far constrained their technological application. In this work, we perform a high-throughput computational search for semiconducting chiral compounds in the cubic space group $P4_332$ (No. 212). By integrating machine-learning techniques with density functional theory, we obtain 24\,227 cubic chiral structures containing up to five elements, and identify 368 thermodynamically stable semiconductors on the convex hull and 3\,048 within 50~meV/atom. We analyze their structural motifs, stability, and electronic band structures, highlighting recurring prototype families, several of which show intrinsic intermediate-band features. Our results substantially expand the known phase space of cubic chiral semiconductors and may guide future efforts in the discovery and design of chiral materials.

items.title: Charge-tunable acoustic surface plasmons in topological nodal-line semimetals
items.summary: Topological nodal-line semimetals host drumhead surface states, carrying a large surface density of states. We show that these states support an acoustic surface plasmon, whose velocity is strongly enhanced by the Coulomb interaction. At sufficiently small wavevectors, the mode lies above the surface particle-hole continuum and below both mixed surface-bulk absorption thresholds, leaving bulk particle-hole creation as the leading damping channel. Near drumhead depletion, the dispersion is highly sensitive to the surface charge, which suggests applications of plasmon spectroscopy of nodal-line semimetals to sensing technologies.

items.title: Dynamical confinement creates quasi-critical scale-free dynamics
items.summary: Scale-free avalanches are commonly interpreted as signatures of criticality. Conventional theoretical frameworks predict robust avalanche-size exponents $τ$ bounded by $3/2$, while dissipation is expected to drive systems away from criticality, by progressively suppressing large events. Yet earthquakes and numerous dissipative experiments exhibit scale-free dynamics with non-universal exponents $τ> 3/2$, challenging both expectations. Using the Olami-Feder-Christensen model as a minimal theoretical framework, we identify two fundamentally distinct routes to scale-free dynamics:a genuinely critical scenario, in which avalanches continuously explore the entire system and remain permanently capable of spanning it; and a quasi-critical scenario, in which dissipation and the traces left by past avalanches generate dynamical confinement. Rather than remaining at a critical point, the system explores a power-law distribution of distances to criticality. We show, using a simple analytical model, how this mechanism produces scale-free avalanche statistics with dissipation-dependent exponents exceeding $τ= 3/2$. Our results establish a physical mechanism for scale-free dynamics beyond conventional criticality, providing a framework for understanding the non-universal avalanche statistics observed in earthquakes and dissipative systems.

items.title: Quantitative Impact of Occupation Smearing Methods on Conventional Superconductivity: from Electronic Structure through Lattice Dynamics to Electron-Phonon Coupling
items.summary: In first-principles calculations of metallic systems, the discrete electronic mesh in the Brillouin zone necessitates a smearing function and its width (e.g., the widely used 0.02 Ry Methfessel-Paxton scheme) to enforce continuity of energy and occupation at the Fermi surface. However, the quantitative impact of such empirical parameters on phonon-mediated superconductivity has long been overlooked, leading to their habitual selection by mere convention. Here, using hexahydride CsH6 as a benchmark, we systematically investigate the magnitude and propagation mechanism of smearing-induced errors against the parameter-free optimized tetrahedron method. Long-tailed smearing delocalizes the occupation window, causing substantial Fermi-level shifts, flattening of the density of states, and hardening phonon modes, thereby weakening electron-phonon coupling. Conversely, short-tailed smearing suffers from insufficient sampling, producing density-of-states oscillations and enhanced Fermi-surface nesting. These artifacts amplify electronic screening and Peierls instabilities, which soften acoustic modes and generate imaginary frequencies, causing CsH6 to be dynamically unstable and discarded. However, the optimized tetrahedron method reveals that CsH6 is dynamically stable under ambient pressure with a remarkable superconducting transition temperature of 121 K. To prevent subjective empirical parameters from obscuring theoretically promising high-temperature superconductors, we derive a simple scaling relation for the smearing width, applicable to different smearing functions, from the free-electron-gas model, offering an objective, precise, and efficient protocol for parameter selection in high-throughput screening.

items.title: Susceptibility-kinetic uncertainty relations for quantum systems
items.summary: Kinetic uncertainty relations bound current precision of stochastic processes by dynamical activity. The extension of these bounds to quantum systems has been impeded by coherence, strong system-reservoir coupling, and the subtlety of defining dynamical activity in the quantum regime. Here, we introduce a partial dynamical activity through the quantum Fisher information associated with the rescaling of the system-reservoir coupling and show that it bounds current precision via a universal susceptibility-kinetic uncertainty relation. The general validity of this relation is guaranteed by the natural contribution of a susceptibility term, which is experimentally accessible by tuning the system-reservoir coupling strength. We show how the partial dynamical activity encompasses previous definitions of activity in the weak-coupling Markovian limit and that it provides an information-geometric interpretation of correlator-based activities. We illustrate the tight constraint on precision that our bound provides with the example of the dynamics of a strongly interacting finite-size system and of steady-state coherent transport through a double quantum dot, where quantum effects invalidate previously developed kinetic uncertainty relations. We expect our bound to provide a powerful tool for optimizing precision in arbitrary quantum systems.

items.title: Critical geometry of triconnected clusters in percolation
items.summary: We investigate the critical geometry of triconnected clusters in percolation, which remain connected after the removal of any two sites. By combining biconnected-component decomposition with the SPQR decomposition of graphs, we develop an efficient algorithm for identifying triconnected clusters in large systems. Extensive Monte Carlo simulations yield estimates of the fractal dimension $d_3=1.2308(3)$, $1.083(2)$, and $0.77(2)$ in dimensions $d=2$, $3$, and $4$, respectively, revealing a systematic decrease of $d_3$ with increasing $d$. In dimension $d=6$, the largest triconnected cluster grows logarithmically with system size, whereas on complete graphs, corresponding to $d=\infty$, it approaches a finite size. Both behaviors indicate a vanishing fractal dimension, $d_3=0$, for $d\geq6$. Furthermore, the singular contribution to the susceptibility-like quantity associated with the second moment of the triconnected-cluster size distribution scales as $χ\sim L^{2d_3-d}$. Consequently, it vanishes for $d\geq3$, leaving a finite asymptotic susceptibility, in contrast to the divergent behavior observed in standard percolation.

items.title: Making Plasticity Visible: A Case Study for High-Temperature Exposed Aluminum Alloy
items.summary: Understanding the onset of plastic deformation and the early development of strain localization is essential for characterizing material behavior and identifying failure-prone regions. However, these transitions are not always distinguishable from conventional full-field strain measurements. This study investigates a data- driven framework combining Digital Image Correlation (DIC) and Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to extract temporal and spatial deformation signatures during uniaxial tensile loading. The methodology is evaluated using AA6063-T5 aluminum alloy specimens in the as-received condition and following thermal exposure at 100~$^\circ$C, 200~$^\circ$C, and 300~$^\circ$C. PCA applied to sequential strain fields reveals a characteristic peak in the second principal component projection near the yielding transition, showing agreement with the conventional 0.2\% offset criterion across the investigated conditions. Furthermore, principal component maps extracted from high-temporal-resolution strain fields preceding this transition highlight localized deformation features associated with subsequent failure regions. These features are more clearly distinguishable than competing strain concentrations in the corresponding instantaneous strain maps. The results indicate that PCA-derived deformation signatures remain identifiable despite thermally induced variations in mechanical response. This approach demonstrates the potential of unsupervised dimensionality reduction for extracting physically interpretable information on plastic deformation and early strain localization from experimental full-field measurements.

items.title: Pressure dependent DFT study of mechanical, thermal, electronic, magnetic, and optical properties of EuCd2As2: a magnetic semimetal
items.summary: We present a comprehensive spin-polarized density functional theory (DFT) investigation of the pressure-dependent physical properties of EuCd2As2, a magnetically and topologically rich compound with potential applications in spintronics and optoelectronics technologies. We have investigated the structural, mechanical, thermophysical, acoustic, electronic, magnetic, and optical properties of this material at pressures of 0, 2, 4, 6, and 8 GPa. The calculated lattice parameters at zero pressure are in good agreement with experimental values. The mechanical stability of EuCd2As2 is maintained over the investigated pressure range. The elastic constants, bulk modulus, shear modulus, and Young's modulus are found to be tunable with applied pressure. The compound undergoes a brittle to ductile transition at higher pressures. The Debye temperature, melting temperature, and Grüneisen parameter are found to be strongly pressure-dependent. Phonon thermal conductivity has been evaluated. The electronic properties of EuCd2As2 were studied through band structure and density of states (DOS). The effect of pressure up to 8 GPa was investigated for the ferromagnetic (FM) phase. At 0 GPa, the calculated FM band structure exhibits no band gap at the Fermi level, which confirms the semimetallic nature of EuCd2As2. The net magnetic moment of 6.96 μ_B per unit cell was obtained for this compound indicating its potential for spintronics application. The optical properties, including the dielectric function, refractive index, absorption coefficient, optical conductivity, reflectivity, and loss function, are calculated. The calculated optical spectra indicate strong absorption in the visible and ultraviolet regions, suggesting that EuCd2As2 may have potential for optoelectronic applications.

items.title: Vestiges of magnon fractionalization in the quasi-two-dimensional quantum magnet rouaite Cu$_2$(NO$_3$)(OH)$_3$ with alternating ferro- and antiferromagnetic $S=\frac{1}{2}$ chains
items.summary: Ferro- and antiferromagnetic quantum spin chains host qualitatively distinct elementary excitations --- magnons ($S=1$, bosonic quasiparticles) and spinons ($S=\frac{1}{2}$, fractionalized quasiparticles), respectively. Weakly coupled networks of both chain types therefore provide an ideal platform for exploring spinon-magnon coupling and the hybridization of sharp magnon modes with spinon continua. Here we investigate the spin-excitation spectrum of the frustrated quantum magnet rouaite, Cu$_2$(NO$_3$)(OH)$_3$ --- a model realization of weakly coupled ferro- and antiferromagnetic Cu$^{2+}$ spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ chains. The frustrated interchain interactions, while weaker than the dominant intrachain exchange, are sufficient to stabilize a long-range-ordered state that is not reproduced by classical calculations. Neutron spectroscopy reveals a spectrum of well-defined spin waves associated with both types of chains, with clear signatures of hybridization but no observable spinon continuum. Certain magnon branches resulting from this hybridization exhibit substantial broadening near the zone center. We attribute this to vestiges of spinon fractionalization persisting partway through the dimensional crossover from isolated quantum spin chains to a 2D network of frustrated spins.

items.title: Exact stochastic theory of post-transcriptional gene autoregulation mediated by RNA-binding proteins
items.summary: While analytical theories of transcriptional feedback loops have been well established, exact stochastic analyses of post-transcriptional feedback loops remain relatively scarce and are notoriously challenging. Here, we develop an exact theory of post-transcriptional gene autoregulation, in which reversible protein-mRNA binding modulates both translation and mRNA stability. We derive the state-dependent protein burst-size distribution, the steady-state protein number distribution in terms of confluent Heun functions, and an exact criterion for sub-Poissonian fluctuations. By comparing transcriptional and post-transcriptional networks, we reveal a reversal in their relative advantages in noise suppression and rhythm transmission: negative feedback favors post-transcriptional regulation, whereas positive feedback favors transcriptional regulation. Our results reveal how the regulatory pattern fundamentally shapes gene expression fluctuations and dynamic responses.

items.title: Consensus in Effective Model Inference for Disordered Ising Systems
items.summary: When independent learners are trained on data from the same disordered system, finite and noisy samples can lead them to different descriptions of the underlying physics. We quantify the reproducibility of such descriptions through consensus, the degree of agreement among independently trained models. In a teacher-student framework on the two-dimensional random-bond Ising model, an ensemble of students each infers a single uniform effective coupling from a finite set of equilibrium configurations drawn from one quenched bond realization. Aggregating the inferred couplings across students and realizations yields the consensus distribution, whose width quantifies the agreement among learners. The variance of this distribution separates exactly into a finite-sampling contribution, bounded below by inverse of Fisher information, and a quenched-disorder contribution. Sum of these two variance is minimized near critical region, so the consensus width has a minimum near the pseudocritical temperature that sharpens with increasing disorder. The two minima arise from different mechanisms: the sampling term inherits the critical peak of the Fisher information, while the disorder term is temperature-independent at leading order and acquires its critical minimum only at fourth order in the disorder strength, through the covariance between the linear and cubic responses to the bond disorder. Because the students fit a uniform coupling to a heterogeneous lattice, the inferred coupling also carries a misspecification bias that survives in the infinite-data limit. This bias displaces the minimum of the mean-squared error above the consensus minimum, so the temperature at which independent learners agree most closely is not the temperature at which their shared answer is most faithful.

items.title: Connecting finite-size scaling and renormalization-group flows in Anderson localization on random graphs
items.summary: We investigate the relation between two complementary descriptions of the Anderson transition on small-world random graphs: finite-size scaling of eigenfunction moments and renormalization-group (RG) flows of multifractal dimensions $D_q$. The RG flows recover the qualitative structure previously reported for the information dimension $D_1$, while their extension to other $D_q$ with smaller moment orders $q<1/2$ confirms the strongly multifractal nature of the localized phase characterized by a clear distinction between multifractal and localized scaling behaviors of different moments within the localized phase. On the other hand, we show that we can construct another beta function characterizing the flow of eigenfunction moments, whose collapse onto a single function across different disorder strengths supports single-parameter scaling of the normalized moments within each sector. These results raise an interesting question about the interpretation of two-parameter scaling: while a two-dimensional flow structure has been inferred from the information dimension $D_1$ alone, our analysis reveals two distinct scaling sectors by considering different eigenfunction moments. To characterize these properties, one should consider different observables, such as large $q>1/2$ and small $q<1/2$ eigenfunction moments, which are associated with distinct critical behaviors, in particular different critical exponents.

items.title: Ultralow Lattice Thermal Conductivity in Orthorhombic Rb2Se3 with rigid covalent trimers and a soft ionic framework
items.summary: Alkali-metal-containing compounds often exhibit exceptionally low lattice thermal conductivity, yet the structural origins and transport mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigate orthorhombic Rb2Se3 using first-principles bonding, lattice-dynamical, and thermal-transport calculations. Bonding analyses reveal strongly covalent, V-shaped Se3 trimers embedded in a soft ionic coordination framework. Representing each trimer as a pseudo-atom reveals a pseudo-one-dimensional chain arrangement along [001] within the three-dimensional crystal.This bonding hierarchy produces a dense low-frequency phonon manifold and four separated high-frequency optical branches dominated by internal trimer stretching. Four-phonon scattering strongly suppresses particle-like heat transport, leaving the coherent contribution dominant. The coherent contribution is largest along the pseudo-atom-chain direction [001] and accounts for most of the thermal conductivity anisotropy. At 300 K, the total lattice thermal conductivities are 0.067, 0.096, and 0.265 W/mK along [100], [010], and [001], respectively. These results connect the coexistence of rigid covalent trimers and a soft ionic framework to ultra-low thermal conductivity, while revealing how their structural arrangement is reflected in directional coherent heat transfer.

items.title: Comment on "Kinematic and Rheological Equivalence of Steady Shearing and Planar Extensional Flows"
items.summary: In Reference [Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 144003 (2026)], the authors claim the 'kinematic' and 'rheological' equivalence between simple shear and planar extension. They state that their result holds "for any materially objective constitutive equation." The proposed relation is exact for single-mode constitutive models whose stress is coaxial with a single tensor obeying an evolution equation that depends linearly on the velocity gradient. However, it fails for standard kinetic theories of dilute solutions, e.g. FENE dumbbells, and for the integral tube or K-BKZ models of entangled solutions and melts. Their result is a consequence of the employed closures, not of an underlying equivalence between the flows. Its accuracy for real fluids cannot be inferred from such closed models and instead requires independent validation against measured planar extensional data.

items.title: Tunable Valley Filtering and Splitting via Gate Control in Wrinkled Graphene
items.summary: We investigate the use of strain-induced wrinkles in graphene nanoribbons to achieve tunable valley filtering and splitting, crucial for advancing valleytronic devices. By combining tight-binding simulations, strain tensor analysis, and quantum transport calculations, we explicitly demonstrate that wrinkle-induced pseudomagnetic fields facilitate current splitting and valley-selective filtering in folded graphene nanoribbons based on wrinkle parameters like height, strain spreading/deformation and wrinkle orientation (tilt angle). Moreover, we show that the application of a top-gate voltage provides dynamic control over valley splitting, allowing a continuous transition from well-separated valley currents to valley merging as the gate voltage increases. In other parameter regimes, valley filtering arises from an initial current-splitting mechanism, exhibiting a clear gate-controlled transition between distinct transport behaviors. Our results offer new insights into strain-engineered valley transport and suggest a promising pathway toward practical graphene-based valleytronic devices.

items.title: A Machine-learning-aided Workflow for Sampling Small Polaron Dynamics in Energy Materials
items.summary: One of the defining characteristics of most energy materials, used as e.g.~battery electrodes, photovoltaics, or photocatalysts, is their ability conduct charges such as electrons and holes. The exact mechanism of this conductivity depends on the material, but is often dominated by the existence of mobile small polarons, i.e.~electrons or holes strongly localised through the polarisation of their environment. Computationally, small polarons can be treated with reasonably accuracy through the use of self-interaction corrected or hybrid density functional theory (DFT) together with local geometry optimisation. Similar approaches can be employed to determine the energy barriers to movement of the polarons through hopping. Unfortunately, realistic energy materials tend have very large numbers of symmetry inequivalent polaronic configurations and correspondingly large numbers of hopping barriers, making them hard to tackle explicitly. In this work we therefore extend the computational reach of DFT calculations with machine-learned (ML) surrogate models, which then feed into a kinetic model to quantitatively estimate the conductivity of a battery anode material (Li$_4$Ti$_5$O$_12$ or LTO) at realistic, defected conditions. We calculate the conductivity at room temperature to be 6.7 $\times$ 10$^{-3}$ S/cm which lies well in the experimental range. To this end, we only needed a total of 154 polaron barrier calculations, out of 3649 symmetry inequivalent ones, achieving an over 20-fold increase of computational efficiency. Overall, our work demonstrates how DFT-trained ML surrogates can be used to quantitatively and efficiently sample the dynamics of small polarons in energy materials.

items.title: Quantum kinetic uncertainty relations: Role of coherence in current fluctuation bounds
items.summary: We present a comparative analysis of three quantum versions of the kinetic uncertainty relation (KUR), which incorporate coherence-dependent corrections to the classical bound. Using a three-level maser heat engine as a paradigmatic quantum thermal machine, we identify the operating regimes in which each formulation provides the tightest constraint on current fluctuations. We further identify tighter, model-specific bounds for two of these formulations, provide numerical support for both, and establish one of them analytically. Introducing ground-state degeneracy, we then demonstrate that noise-induced coherence provides a tunable resource for relocating, enhancing, or suppressing violations of the standard KUR without requiring an additional coherent drive. In particular, it enables violations in regimes where the three-level engine satisfies the classical bound. Our results clarify how distinct quantum KURs account for coherence and constrain the precision of quantum thermal machines.

items.title: Charge and spin orders of the generalized Wigner crystal phases at fractional fillings in twisted MoTe$_2$: unrestricted Hartree-Fock and variational Monte Carlo studies
items.summary: Recent experiments have revealed interaction-driven insulating states at various fractional fillings of twisted bilayer MoTe$_2$. Many of these insulating states are believed to be generalized Wigner crystals (GWC) condensed in the background of triangular moir$\acute{e}$ lattice. In this work, we focus on revealing the charge and spin order of the insulating states at 4/3 and 3/2 hole fillings over a range of twist angles and applied displacement fields using unrestricted Hartree-Fock (HF) and variational Monte Carlo (VMC) methods. We find that, at 4/3 filling for low twist angles the charge ordered ground state is valley-polarized (VP), characterized by weak charge delocalization approaching the classical limit. Application of the displacement field induces layer-polarization and suppresses the charge fluctuations even further. In contrast, at 3/2 filling, the VP phase exhibits signatures of a two-component GWC phase, which is particularly robust at finite displacement field. Additionally, by increasing the twist angle one pushes the system into an intervalley-coherent (IVC) phase, which is found to be fluctuation-dominated. Our VMC-based analysis shows that the correlation energy is negligible in the VP phase, which is consistent with its classical nature. However, the IVC phase shows significant gain in correlation energy, which is dominated by the nonlocal correlations captured by the Jastrow factors, while the local Gutzwiller factors play a minor role.

items.title: A Cantilever-Based Method for Probing Adhesion Force and Kinetic Detachment Energy in Cohesive Granular Materials
items.summary: Interparticle adhesion plays a critical role in the flow behavior of cohesive granular materials, yet quantitative characterization at the particle scale remains challenging. Here, we present a cantilever-based method that combines a glass-beam cantilever for force measurements with a novel catapult mode for energy measurements, enabling the determination of both quasi-static detachment force and kinetic detachment energy. Applied to three different cohesive materials: polymer-coated silica particles, wet granular media, and cross-linked poly(2-ethylhexyl acrylate) (PEHA) microparticles, this method reveals a fundamental decoupling between force and energy, suggesting that both quantities are equally critical for characterizing grain properties.

items.title: Two correlation scales in homogeneous density-matrix functionals: the Müller logarithm and the sharp Csányi--Arias asymptotics
items.summary: We resolve the exact high-density correlation scales and coefficients of the three-dimensional translation-invariant, spin-symmetric Müller and Csányi--Arias corrected Hartree--Fock (CHF) functionals, settling long-standing numerical observations of Müller overcorrelation and apparently vanishing CHF correlation. In Hartree units, for fixed spin multiplicity $q$ and Fermi momentum $k=(6π^2ρ/q)^{1/3}$, their gains per particle over the filled Fermi sea satisfy \[ D_{\rm M}(k)=\frac{3}{4π^2}\log k+O(1),\qquad D_{\rm CHF}(k)=12e^{-1/2-π^2/8} k^2e^{-π^{3/2}\sqrt{k}}(1+o(1)). \] The Müller proof retains the occupation cap and identifies the factor-of-two cancellation between exchange defect and energy gain. For periodic Müller jellium, convexity and translation--spin averaging allow a global minimizer to be chosen invariant and identify the unrestricted thermodynamic energy with the homogeneous spin-symmetric value. The CHF upper bound follows from a deterministic comparison built from the explicit Hartree--Fock dispersion, combining a full Birman--Schwinger bound with one-sided norms and completion of the square; a number-preserving trial state provides the matching lower bound, and the retained remainder yields weighted $L^2$ convergence of the occupation defect without analyzing the self-consistent gap. We also prove existence for both functionals and uniqueness of the CHF minimizer. Relative to the unpolarized quantum high-density benchmark, Müller has a larger logarithmic coefficient, providing quantitative evidence for the conjectured Müller lower-bound property, whereas CHF misses the logarithmic scale altogether. The quantum benchmark is not used in either functional proof.

items.title: Low-Temperature Heat Capacity of Single-Walled Carbon Nanotube Bundles with low dimensional gas systems
items.summary: Low-temperature heat-capacity data for pristine single-walled carbon nanotube (SWCNT) bundles and for SWCNT/gas systems containing adsorbed Xe, Ne, N2, and CH4 were analyzed within a phenomenological framework. The data were fitted within the phenomenological form C(T) = C3T3 + C5T5, where the coefficients are interpreted as effective parameters of the coupled SWCNT-adsorbate excitation spectrum. Pristine SWCNT bundles exhibit a negative C5 coefficient, reflecting a non-Debye dispersive contribution associated with low-energy flexural-like modes. Gas adsorption systematically modifies both C3 and C5, indicating that the adsorbate's heat-capacity contribution may not be treated as fully independent. The Xe series suggests that mass loading, modified adsorbate-nanotube interaction, and changes in intertube coupling slightly reshape the nanotube vibrational response. Coverage-dependent measurements for Ne reveal a progressive shift from nanotube-dominated excitations toward domination of additional low-energy adsorbate modes in the phonon spectrum of the SWCNT-Ne system, while molecular adsorbates (N2, CH4) introduce translational, librational, orientational, and rotational degrees of freedom that generate correspondingly stronger perturbations.

items.title: Analytical treatment of reentrant localization via Lyapunov branch structure
items.summary: In reentrant localization, states become localized under a growing quasiperiodic potential partly become extended again before localizing once more. So far this has been demonstrated only numerically. Here we prove it in a chain of weakly coupled dimers in which we vary only the overall strength of a fixed onsite potential. As the strength increases, the lower orbital of each dimer shifts its weight between the two sites. At a particular strength, the quasiperiodic potential it feels cancels, while the hopping between dimers stays finite. When the energy scales are well separated, we prove that, over a finite range of potential strengths, all states in a central part of the lower band, one third of its states, have a vanishing Lyapunov exponent that is stable against small changes of phase, the certification of extended states. On both sides of this range, all states are localized. Numerical calculations confirm that the recovery covers the whole lower band, while the upper band stays localized.

items.title: Emulating spatially extended systems using Fourier Neural Operator
items.summary: Operator Learning (OL) algorithms approximate underlying mathematical operators by mapping entire classes of input functions to their corresponding solutions. For instance, architectures such as the Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) have been trained on numerical datasets generated by isolated, stiff ionic models to provide a data-driven alternative to traditional numerical integration schemes. However, real-world biological and physical systems typically consist of interconnected spatial units arranged in complex, heterogeneous networks. Motivated by this observation, we generalize this data-driven framework to spatially extended systems defined on diverse graph topologies, ranging from Erdos-Renyi to Barabasi-Albert networks. Furthermore, we evaluate the proposed approach on empirical data, demonstrating its ability to accurately and efficiently model task-oriented neural activity.

items.title: Reentrant Nematicity from Landau Quantization near a Pomeranchuk Instability
items.summary: Landau quantization can induce nematic order in a two-dimensional Fermi liquid that is isotropic at zero magnetic field. Using a mean-field theory near a quadrupolar Pomeranchuk instability, we show that varying the magnetic field produces alternating nematic and isotropic regions, with transitions that can be either continuous or first order. The resulting nematic state also leaves distinctive signatures in the de Haas--van Alphen oscillations. At fixed chemical potential, the field-dependent deformation of the Fermi surface can produce substantial changes in the oscillation frequency, even when the cyclotron mass varies only modestly. At fixed particle density, conservation of the Fermi-surface area preserves the leading oscillation frequency, while the cyclotron mass and harmonic amplitudes remain sensitive to nematic order. These contrasting behaviors provide experimentally relevant signatures of field-induced nematicity and reveal the importance of thermodynamic constraints in quantum-oscillation measurements.

items.title: The de Haas--van Alphen effect in a two-dimensional nematic Fermi fluid
items.summary: Quantum oscillations are widely used to probe the Fermi surface of metals, but their behavior becomes more complex when electronic interactions can spontaneously deform that surface. We investigate this interplay in a two-dimensional model of interacting electrons capable of developing nematic order, using a uniform mean-field approximation in a perpendicular magnetic field. We show that Landau quantization can favor or suppress nematic order as the field varies, producing alternating isotropic and nematic regions near a Pomeranchuk instability, with both continuous and first-order transitions. Conversely, the evolving nematic order modifies the de Haas--van Alphen oscillations in ways that depend on the thermodynamic conditions. At fixed chemical potential, the oscillation frequency can change significantly even when the cyclotron mass varies only modestly. At fixed particle density, conservation of the Fermi-surface area preserves the leading Onsager frequency, while the cyclotron mass and harmonic amplitudes remain sensitive to nematic order. The magnetization and magnetic susceptibility provide additional signatures of the nematic transitions. These results show how quantum oscillations can both reveal and influence electronic order, offering a framework for interpreting experiments in strongly correlated metals.

items.title: Shape of semiflexible polymer chains: Lévy walks vs. Persistent random walks
items.summary: The conformational size and shape characteristics of semiflexible polymer chains, modeled via two distinct frameworks: persistent random walks (PRW) and Lévy walks (LW), are analyzed through numerical simulations. We introduce a mapping that treats the mean jump length $\langle \ell \rangle$ of a Lévy distribution ($\sim \ell^{-(1+σ)}$) as an effective persistence length of the semiflexible polymer chain, controlled by the exponent $σ$. While the conformational characteristics of the PRW model statistically exhibit a sharp crossover from flexible coil to the rigid-rod-like behavior in the immediate vicinity of the maximum persistence probability $p \to 1$, the LW model shows a much richer conformational behavior. We obtain the quantitative estimates for universal shape parameters, such as asphericity \(\langle A_3 \rangle\) and prolateness \(\langle S \rangle\), which gradually increase with decreasing parameter $σ$ (and thus with an increase of the persistence length), thus supporting previously observed findings for semiflexible polymers. Our results demonstrate the effictiveness of applying Lévy-walk statistics to capture the universal conformational properties of semiflexible polymer structures.

items.title: Epitaxial integration of GaN $μ$-platelets and thin films on metallic TiN using a hybrid approach
items.summary: We demonstrate the synthesis of epitaxial, self-organized GaN $μ$-platelets on metallic TiN thin films. To this end, we first nucleate self-assembled GaN nanowires with number densities between 0.01 to 300 $μm^{-2}$ by molecular beam epitaxy. Subsequent overgrowth of these seed nanowires by metal-organic vapor phase epitaxy yields GaN $μ$-platelets with corresponding number densities. The platelets exhibit N-polarity and form an ohmic contact to the metallic TiN substrate. By adjusting the growth conditions during the metal-organic vapor phase epitaxy, particularly the carrier gas and precursor ratio, the morphology of the GaN can be controlled across a broad range. Growth under N$_{2}$ carrier gas and with a 1:1 NH$_{3}$/trimethylgallium precursor flow ratio results in platelet ensembles with broad diameter and height distributions. In contrast, employing an N$_{2}$/H$_{2}$ carrier gas mixture promotes the formation of more homogeneous ensembles with narrower size distributions around a diameter of $\approx$2 $μm$. Finally, N-rich growth conditions under H$_{2}$ carrier gas enhance lateral growth, leading to the formation of coalesced GaN layers. GaN grown under these latter conditions exhibits strong near-band-edge emission, accompanied by only weak deep-level luminescence at room temperature.

items.title: Correlating orbital order and photovoltaic effect in Layered Ruddlesden-Popper Pr0.5Ca1.5MnO4 and PrCa2Mn2O7
items.summary: The understanding of growth and structure-property relations of epitaxial thin films of layered Ruddlesden-Popper perovskite oxides open up new pathways to tune correlated electron properties and to fabricate new types of correlated electron junctions, such as e.g. photovoltaic devices. In particular, the layered Ruddlesden-Popper systems Pr$_0.5$Ca$_1.5$MnO$_4$ and PrCa$_2$Mn$_2$O$_7$ at half doping exhibit much higher transition temperatures for the formation of charge and orbital ordered phases of $T_c$ = 320 K and $T_c$ up to 370 K, respectively, compared to the half doped non-layered system Pr$_{1-x}$Ca$_{x}$MnO$_3$ (PCMO) with $T_c$ = 240 K. Here, we demonstrate the successful growth of epitaxial PrCa$_2$Mn$_2$O$_7$ thin films by ion beam sputtering and compare electric transport, optical absorbance, electronic bandstructure and photovoltaic response with epitaxial Pr$_0.5$Ca$_1.5$MnO$_4$, both deposited on (Nb:)SrTiO$_3$ (110) substrates. An enhanced density of Ruddlesden-Popper type of stacking faults is identified as a relaxation channel for misfit strain in PrCa$_2$Mn$_2$O$_7$ and seems to be the origin for the reduced $T_c$ = 320 K and the reduced spatial coherence of charge and orbital order in comparison to Pr$_0.5$Ca$_1.5$MnO$_4$. Since the onset of the hot polaron photovoltaic effect is correlated to the formation of charge and orbital ordering, the comparative study of temperature dependent electric transport and photovoltaic response gives insights into the different role of strain and strain relaxation related defects on photo-electric properties.

items.title: Universal TT- and TQ-relations via centrally extended q-Onsager algebra
items.summary: Let $A_q$ be the alternating central extension of the q-Onsager algebra, a comodule algebra over the quantum loop algebra of $sl_2$. We classify one-dimensional representations of $A_q$, and show that spin-j K-operators constructed in arXiv:2301.00781 act as K-matrices previously obtained in the literature. Using these K-operators and K-matrices, we construct universal spin-j transfer matrices generating commutative subalgebras in $A_q$. Within a technical conjecture, we derive their fusion hierarchy, the so-called universal TT-relations. On spin-chain representations of $A_q$, we show how the universal transfer matrices evaluate to spin-chain transfer matrices, and as a result we get explicit TT-relations for all values of spins for auxiliary and quantum spaces, any inhomogeneities, and general integrable boundary conditions. In particular, we derive previously conjectured TT-relations. Using the TT-relations, we show that n-th local conserved quantities of the spin-j chains of length N are polynomials of total degree 4Njn in two non-local operators of the q-Onsager algebra. As a result, we give an algorithm of explicit calculation of all local conserved quantities in terms of spin operators. Furthermore, using the universal TT-relations we derive exchange relations between spin-j Hamiltonians and the two non-local operators showing non-trivial symmetries for special boundary conditions, that they commute with all Hamiltonian densities. As another application of our universal TT-relations we propose universal T-system, Y-system and universal TQ-relations for $A_q$, and as a result, universal TQ for the q-Onsager algebra. For diagonal boundary conditions, we also obtain universal TT- and TQ-relations for a degenerate version of $A_q$ known as centrally extended augmented q-Onsager algebra. We finally discuss implications of our results for generalized Gibbs ensemble construction.

items.title: A Multiobjective Optimization Framework for Sensor Array Design in Magnetocardiography
items.summary: Magnetocardiography (MCG) noninvasively measures cardiac magnetic fields. Conventional cryogenic systems use fixed multichannel arrays, whereas room-temperature sensors enable flexible placement to reduce array size and measurement redundancy. The present study aims at developing a scheme to identify the optimal sensor placements by utilizing three methodological sensor optimization frameworks such as physics driven, experimental data driven and a hybrid combination of both. The physics-driven method optimizes continuous planar coordinates using D-optimality, spatial correlation, and leastsquares error. The data-driven method uses measured spatiotemporal fields and pole-geometry metrics, while the hybrid method integrates both approaches. The evaluation is performed using training objective, Pearson correlation, normalized root-meansquare error (NRMSE) and pole separation(mm), orientation(°) and trajectory(mm) errors, where physics-driven optimization identified 16 sensors with a correlation of 0.9914 and an NRMSE of 0.0139, with pole separation, orientation, and trajectory errors of 3.71 mm, 1.38°, and 3.55 mm, respectively. Data-driven optimization shows diminishing improvements beyond 17 sensors, achieving correlation 0.9840, NRMSE 0.0035, and pole errors of approximately 4.30 mm, 1.70°, and 6.80 mm. The hybrid method achieves correlation 0.9945 and NRMSE 0.0201 with 14 sensors, reducing sensor count by 12.5% relative to the physics-driven configuration. Its pole errors of 6.50 mm, 2.31°, and 7.50 mm satisfy the study-defined thresholds, balancing array compactness with magnetic-field morphology preservation. These results show that optimized placement helps alleviate the complexity of data redundancy and enhances the performance of MCG as a routine cost-effective clinical measurement.

items.title: An infrared divacancy color center in bulk hexagonal diamond for quantum communication
items.summary: We investigate intrinsic color centers in bulk hexagonal diamond as potential emitters for fiber-based quantum communication. Hybrid density functional theory and constrained-occupation ΔSCF calcula-tions identify five carbon-vacancy and divacancy configurations with stable optical excited states. Com-paring their radiative and nonradiative properties within a three-point configuration-coordinate model identifies the positively charged axial divacancy, VVa1+, as the most promising candidate. It has the high-est calculated zero-phonon-line (ZPL) emission rate (43.9 MHz) and ZPL quantum efficiency (11.8%) among the five candidates. Its weak structural relaxation gives a Huang-Rhys factor of 0.395, while a mul-timode photoluminescence calculation predicts a Debye-Waller factor of 69.37% and a dominant zero-phonon contribution. Its predicted ZPL at 0.603 eV (2057.3 nm) is also closest in photon energy to the 1310 and 1550 nm telecom targets. Quantum frequency upconversion could connect this strong infrared ZPL to the telecom O and C bands, providing a route toward fiber-based quantum communication with an intrinsic color center.

items.title: Local electronic structure of the Co2+ ions in the disordered perovskite phase of Ba3CoNb2O9: a temperature-dependent X-ray absorption and magnetic circular dichroism study

We employed the line-fitting inverse partial fluorescence yield (iPFY) method to obtain reliable spectra from this insulating material. From the comparison between the experimental spectra and full multiplet cluster calculations we were able to constrain the local crystal-field environment and assess the spin-orbit-entangled nature of the Co$^{2+}$ ground state. In this chemically disordered system, the Co$^{2+}$ ions retain on average an effectively cubic crystal-field environment that supports a $J_\mathrm{eff} = 1/2$ ground state. These results further establish that Ba$_3$CoNb$_2$O$_9$ is a promising platform for investigating the effect of disorder on $J_\mathrm{eff} = 1/2$ magnetism.

items.title: Efficient ensemble randomization by tuning chaos in a nonlinear spin-1 system
items.summary: We present an efficient scheme to randomize a spin-state ensemble in a nonlinear spin-1 system by tuning chaos with an external periodic drive. Without modulation, the system exhibits a mixed phase space featuring regular islands embedded in a chaotic sea, where global mixing is inhibited by energy conservation. Using numerical simulations, we demonstrate that modulation of a linear Zeeman field not only facilitates transport between different energy shells but also drives ensembles toward a Haar-random distribution over spin states. Under optimized conditions, complete randomization at the level of the second moment is achieved on a timescale set by the inverse nonlinear interaction energy. In the overdriven regime, randomization is unexpectedly suppressed at specific modulation amplitudes, accompanied by the formation of sticky regions in phase space. We attribute this behavior to the dynamical cancellation of the leading low-order harmonic component of the periodic drive. These results illustrate how time-periodic driving can be used to engineer chaotic systems and achieve controllable randomization in nonlinear spin systems.

items.title: Influence of interfacial roughness amplitude and periodicity on giant chiral asymmetry of domain wall mobility in epitaxial Cu/Pd/Co/Pd(111) films
items.summary: We investigate the influence of interfacial roughness amplitude and lateral periodicity on the chirality-dependent mobility of domain walls (DWs) in epitaxial Si(111)/Cu(2-7 nm)/Pd(3 nm)/Co(0.7 nm)/Pd(3 nm) heterostructures. By varying the Cu buffer layer thickness, we systematically modify the morphology of the magnetic interfaces while maintaining a constant composition and thickness of the Pd/Co/Pd trilayer. Scanning tunneling microscopy reveals that increasing the Cu thickness leads to the development of a hierarchical interfacial morphology characterized by increasing roughness amplitude and lateral periodicity. We observe a dramatic enhancement of the asymmetry between the velocities of DWs with opposite chirality in the creep regime, reaching a velocity ratio of approximately 50000 in the sample with a 7-nm-thick Cu buffer layer. This value exceeds by more than an order of magnitude the effective saturated asymmetry previously observed in Pd/Co/Pd structures with roughness controlled by the bottom Pd layer thickness. Despite comparable root-mean-square interface roughness in both series, the Cu-buffer-induced morphology exhibits a substantially larger characteristic lateral periodicity. We propose that the enhanced asymmetry originates from the different spatial organization of interfacial disorder, which modifies the pinning energy landscape and amplifies chirality-dependent thermally activated DW propagation. Our results suggest that engineering not only the amplitude but also the lateral spatial correlations of interfacial roughness provides an effective approach for controlling chiral DW dynamics in magnetic heterostructures.

items.title: Classical weak antilocalization in electron hydrodynamics
items.summary: Weak localization is strongly suppressed in electron hydrodynamics, where frequent electron--electron collisions rapidly dephase the Cooperon. Nevertheless, disorder can still produce a logarithmic correction to the bare hydrodynamic resistivity. We show that spatial fluctuations of the momentum-relaxation rate generate a classical memory kernel through the diffusive return of transverse momentum. In two dimensions, this return is logarithmic, as in weak localization, but involves a single shear propagator rather than quantum interference. Conservation laws and positivity of dissipation fix its antilocalizing sign: the return reduces momentum relaxation and hence the bulk resistivity. Unlike quantum weak localization, the logarithm is cut off by momentum relaxation and has a viscosity-dependent amplitude. For temperature-independent impurity friction, the resistivity correction scales as $-T^2\ln(T_ξ/T)$ in a Fermi liquid and $-T\ln(T_ξ/T)$ in a Planckian metal. In channels, the return competes with viscosity renormalization, and a width scan separates the two effects.

items.title: Digital dissipative state preparation for frustration-free gapless quantum systems
items.summary: Preparing algebraically correlated ground states of quantum many-body systems is an important, yet challenging task for quantum simulation. We introduce a protocol that employs local projective measurements and unitary feedback for frustration-free gapless systems. Our approach prepares a priori unknown ground states in time that scales polynomially with system size. We analytically show the performance of our protocol for the dynamics of a single particle; we argue the same mechanism generalizes to many-body systems based on the physics of quasiparticles. Our theory predicts that the transient cooling dynamics directly reveals the system's universal critical properties. In particular, the state preparation time is linear in the inverse of the finite-size gap (up to log correction) when the system's dynamical critical exponent is larger than or equal to the effective spatial dimension explored by the quasiparticles. We verify these predictions in numerical simulations of ferromagnetic Heisenberg models in one- and two dimensions, a Fredkin spin chain, and a two-dimensional model of resonating valence bond states. Our protocol stabilizes gapless many-body ground states fully digitally without requiring analog rotations, enabling access to high-fidelity states beyond conventional adiabatic approaches in near-term experiments.

items.title: The bias interval of the elephant random walk
items.summary: Guérin, Laulin, Raschel, and Simon conjectured that the initial biases giving the superdiffusive elephant random walk a bimodal limit law form an interval centered at one half, and they described the problem as challenging. We prove this. For every superdiffusive memory, strongly biased starts are unimodal, and the limit density has two local maxima exactly when the bias lies in a proper open interval. Outside it, including its endpoints, the density has a unique local maximum. The interval is nonempty exactly above a single memory threshold, numerically about $0.6688$, whose uniqueness follows from a positive-weight integral for the central curvature of the fair-start density. We control sign changes in the finite walk's first and second differences, including those created at the boundary, and pass them to the limit. The bias boundary is continuous and tends to zero at least quadratically fast as memory tends to one.

items.title: Quantum Fluctuations drive Emerging Bosonic Quantum Phases in a Moiré Flatband Superconductor
items.summary: Quantum fluctuations play a central role in superconductors by mediating the interactions that promote electron pairing and controlling the phase coherence required for macroscopic condensation. Thus far, understanding the interplay between quantum fluctuations and superconductivity remains challenging in unconventional superconductors. Here, we establish quantum phase fluctuations as the organizing principle linking superconductivity and Bose-insulating quantum criticality in a moiré flatband superconductor of alternating twisted trilayer graphene (ATTG). Superconductivity is optimal near half-filling of the moiré flatband and gives way to a density-wave-like resistance peak at high temperatures, in which we observe distinct temperature scales for the pairing (~6 K) and the condensation (~1 K). We observe compelling evidence of a bosonic superconducting quantum phase transition, driven by both out-of-plane and in-plane magnetic fields, with a universal critical resistivity of $R_c =~0.62R_Q$ and finite-temperature scaling of $zν_B = 2.3$, where $R_Q = h/4e^2$ is the quantum resistance for bosons. Strikingly, the observed bosonic insulator shows a nearly quantized resistivity of $R_Q$ that saturates at low temperatures and high magnetic fields, together with a zero-bias peak, a nearly zero Hall resistance, and a logarithmic dependence at higher temperatures. Both the superconductor and the bosonic insulator could be driven into the same critical quantum fluctuation regime dynamically under a large bias. Our results establish moiré flatband as a clean platform for studying unconventional superconductivity and bosonic quantum criticality governed by quantum fluctuations.

items.title: Evaluate Laughlin spectral gap lower bound in vortexable bands
items.summary: Vortexable Chern bands admit exact Laughlin-type zero modes of local parent interactions, but their existence alone does not guarantee a finite excitation gap. Here, we derive a computable, particle-number-independent lower bound on the spectral gap of Laughlin parent Hamiltonians in a class of vortexable bands obtained by multiplying lowest-Landau-level wavefunctions by a spatially varying envelope. The bound depends only on two quantities: the spread of projected orbital normalizations and a lower bound on the weighted local pair repulsion, both determined by one- and two-particle operators. The proof employs an auxiliary fermion-loss construction to control orbital orthogonalization, with an error bounded relative to the interaction energy uniformly in particle number. We demonstrate that Landau-level averaging permits strictly positive gap bounds even under substantial spatial modulation, including envelopes with nodal lines. Beyond the scalar-envelope construction, we extend the analysis to multicomponent orbital textures and deformations of the vortex coordinate. These results establish rigorous gap criteria for Laughlin parent Hamiltonians, providing a foundation for understanding the stability of fractional Chern insulators in vortexable bands.
